title: Three letters, and then the Living One speaks.
subtitle: A pause before a long surah begins
then: Ali Imran was revealed in Madinah, and its opening part came around the time of the delegation from Najran. Like Al-Baqarah, it opens with three letters. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} What follows is one of the most powerful statements about Him in the Quran.
now: You open the app on the bus, thumb ready to scroll. Three letters sit there with no translation you can grab onto. {idea}That small gap is the point.{/idea} Your mind slows down before the words about the Living One arrive.
old: If I cannot understand a letter, there is nothing in it for me.
new: Not everything is mine to decode. Some things are there to make me stop and listen.
try: Next time you recite Alif Lam Mim, take one slow breath before you go on.

title: Everything you lean on is held up by Him.
subtitle: The Ever-Living who keeps all things standing
then: Ibn Kathir notes a hadith saying {idea}Allah's Greatest Name is contained in this verse{/idea} and in Ayat al-Kursi, which share the same words. It was revealed in Madinah, where the Muslims met people who believed a created being could be divine.
now: Your phone battery dies. Your manager quits. The doctor calls back with a new number. Everything you leaned on turns out to need support itself. {reward}One does not.{/reward}
old: I am held up by the people and things around me.
new: Everything holding me up is itself held up by the One who never dies.
try: Before sleeping tonight, say Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum three times and name one worry.

title: The Quran did not cancel the old books. It confirmed them.
subtitle: One line of revelation, from Musa to Isa to Muhammad

row.title: one source
sub: each confirms the truth before it

then: The surah speaks to Muslims and to the people of the Book. Ibn Kathir explains the Quran came {idea}with truth, no doubt that it is from Allah{/idea}, and that it confirms the earlier revealed books, which in turn carried news of the Prophet ﷺ to come.
now: Your coworker mentions Moses and Jesus, assuming you see them as someone else's prophets. {reward}They are yours too.{/reward} The book on your phone calls their scriptures guidance from the same Lord.
old: Other faiths' prophets belong to other people.
new: Musa and Isa are part of my own story, sent by the same Lord.
try: Read one short passage about Musa or Isa in the Quran today.

title: The Criterion is how you tell right from wrong.
subtitle: Guidance that separates, and the cost of refusing it
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Criterion as {idea}the distinction between misguidance and guidance, falsehood and truth{/idea}, made clear by the proofs it contains. Those who denied the signs unjustly were warned that Allah is All-Mighty.
now: A friend asks if a side deal is really that bad. Everyone online has an opinion. {idea}You have a measuring line in your pocket{/idea} that does not change with the trend.
old: Right and wrong are mostly a matter of opinion.
new: Allah gave me a criterion so I do not have to guess.
try: Pick one choice you are unsure about this week and look for what the Quran says on it.

title: Nothing on earth or in the sky is hidden from Him.
subtitle: Perfect knowledge, everywhere at once
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}has perfect knowledge in the heavens and earth{/idea}, and nothing in them escapes His watch. The verse prepares for the next one about what happens in the womb.
now: The quiet kindness no one noticed. The tab you closed when someone walked in. Both are equally seen. {reward}The first is not wasted.{/reward} {trap}The second is not secret.{/trap}
old: What nobody sees does not really count.
new: Everything counts, because nothing is hidden from Allah.
try: Do one good thing today that no one will ever find out about.

title: He shaped you in the womb before anyone saw you.
subtitle: Formed as He willed, so He alone is worshipped
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah forms each person in the womb as He wills, male or female, and in every other way. He adds that {idea}Isa son of Mary was also formed in a womb{/idea}, stage by stage, so he is a created servant, not divine.
now: You stand in front of the mirror listing what you would change. {reward}The One who chose your face did it on purpose.{/reward} Your shape was decided with wisdom before your mother saw you.
old: My looks and nature are random, and I wish they were different.
new: I was shaped on purpose, by the Almighty, the Wise.
try: Look in the mirror once today and say alhamdulillah instead of a criticism.

title: Read the unclear in light of the clear.
subtitle: Firm verses, unclear verses, and the hearts that choose
then: Ibn Kathir explains that clear verses are the base, and unclear ones are understood by returning to them. {trap}Those with deviation in their hearts{/trap} grab the unclear to support what they already want. The Prophet ﷺ warned to beware of people who argue this way.
now: A clip goes viral: one verse, cut short, used to prove a strange claim. The comments explode. {idea}The firm in knowledge go back to the clear verses{/idea} and say: all of it is from our Lord.
old: If a verse can be read my way, that settles it.
new: The clear verses are the anchor, and I read everything else through them.
try: When a verse confuses you, read the verses around it before you form a view.

title: Even the guided ask not to drift.
subtitle: The prayer of those firm in knowledge
then: This is the prayer of {idea}those firmly grounded in knowledge{/idea} from the verse before. Right after describing hearts that swerve, the Quran shows the people who stayed straight asking Allah not to let theirs swerve.
now: You have been praying on time for a year. A part of you feels safe now. {trap}Then a hard month comes and the habit slips.{/trap} The ones who last are the ones who keep asking, not the ones who feel finished.
old: I am practicing now, so I am safe.
new: Guidance is a gift I ask to keep, every single day.
try: Memorize this prayer, Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana, and say it after one prayer today.

title: A Day is coming, and He never breaks a promise.
subtitle: Why the firm in knowledge stay firm
then: The prayer of the firm in knowledge continues. They end it by remembering {idea}the Day all people will be gathered{/idea}, and that Allah does not fail in His promise. That certainty is what keeps them steady.
now: The landlord said he would fix the heater. The friend said he would pay you back. You have learned to half-believe promises. {reward}This one is different.{/reward}
old: Promises get broken, so I do not count on any of them.
new: There is one promise I can build my life on.
try: Keep one small promise today that you have been putting off.

title: Wealth and children cannot stand between you and Allah.
subtitle: What people count on that will not help
then: Ibn Kathir explains that those who denied Allah's signs and His messengers will find that {trap}their wealth and offspring will not avail them{/trap} or save them from His punishment. He links it to the warning not to be impressed by their affluence.
now: Payday. You check your balance and feel safe for a moment. Your kids are doing well. {idea}These are blessings, not a shield.{/idea} On that Day, only your faith and deeds stand with you.
old: Money and a good family will cover me if things go wrong.
new: What I own is a test here, not protection before Allah.
try: Spend a little from your wealth today on someone who has less, for Allah alone.

title: Pharaoh's people had a habit. It ended badly.
subtitle: A pattern of denial and how it ends
then: Ibn Kathir notes Ibn Abbas read the word here as {trap}the behavior and habit of Pharaoh's people{/trap}. They and the nations before them rejected the messengers and proofs, and their end was the same.
now: It starts small: ignoring one reminder, then scrolling past the next. {trap}After a while it is just how you are.{/trap} The verse is about habits more than single moments. {idea}Habits can also be turned.{/idea}
old: Ignoring one reminder is no big deal.
new: Repeated ignoring becomes a pattern, and patterns have an end.
try: Notice one reminder you usually brush off, and act on it once today.

title: Being on top today does not mean winning.
subtitle: A warning after Badr

row.title: you will be overcome
sub: here and in the next life

then: Ibn Kathir reports that after victory at Badr, the Prophet ﷺ returned to Madinah and {idea}gathered people in the marketplace of Bani Qaynuqa{/idea} to warn them. Allah told him to say that those who disbelieve will be overcome and gathered to Hell.
now: You see someone get ahead by cutting corners and wonder why you bother. {idea}Today's scoreboard is not the final one.{/idea} The question is not who looks strong now, but where your own road leads.
old: Whoever is winning now must be doing something right.
new: The final result is with Allah, so I watch my own road.
try: Stop comparing yourself to one person today. Make dua for them instead.

title: At Badr, the smaller army won.
subtitle: Help comes from Allah, not from numbers
then: Ibn Kathir explains this refers to the two camps that met at Badr. Each side saw the other as twice its size. {idea}Ibn Mas'ud said they looked twice as many{/idea}, then at the clash each side looked smaller to the other. {reward}Allah gave victory to the weak little force.{/reward}
now: You are the only one in your office who prays. The only one in the family trying to stop gossip. It feels like you against a crowd. {idea}Badr says the count is not what decides it.{/idea}
old: I am outnumbered, so there is no point trying.
new: Allah supports whom He wills, and numbers do not limit Him.
try: Do one right thing today that you avoided because nobody else was doing it.

title: The things you love were made to look beautiful.
subtitle: Real delights, but short ones

picture.label: What the heart is drawn to

then: Ibn Kathir explains these are real delights Allah placed in this life. {idea}Whether they are praised or blamed depends on the purpose.{/idea} Wealth gathered for pride is a test. {reward}Wealth spent on family and good is encouraged.{/reward}
now: You scroll through houses you cannot afford and cars you do not need. The pull is real, and the verse admits it. {idea}The question is what you want them for{/idea}, and whether they are leading you somewhere better.
old: Wanting nice things means I am a bad Muslim.
new: The pull is natural. What matters is what I do with it and where it leads.
try: Pick one thing you want badly and write down why you want it.

title: Shall I tell you about something better?
subtitle: What waits for the mindful, and the greatest part
then: Right after listing the world's delights, the Prophet ﷺ is told to offer something better. Ibn Kathir notes the gardens are eternal, and that {reward}Allah's pleasure descends on them and He is never angry with them again{/reward}, which another verse calls greater still.
now: You finally buy the phone you saved for. A week later it is just a phone. {idea}The verse is not telling you to want less. It is telling you to want more{/idea}, something that does not wear off.
old: Giving up things now means I lose out.
new: I am not losing, I am being offered something far better.
try: When a craving hits today, quietly say: something better is with my Lord.

title: We believed, so forgive us.
subtitle: The mindful lean on faith, not on their record

row.title: we have believed
sub: in You, Your Book, Your Messenger

row.title: so forgive us
sub: and save us from the Fire

then: Ibn Kathir describes these as the pious servants promised the reward just mentioned. They ask, {idea}because of our faith in You, forgive our errors and shortcomings{/idea}, by Your bounty and mercy. They do not present themselves as perfect.
now: You missed Fajr again and feel like a fraud for even asking. {reward}The people Allah praises here are asking for forgiveness too.{/reward} Faith with mistakes is still the ticket to ask.
old: I have messed up too much to ask for forgiveness.
new: Belief is the reason I can ask, not the reason I should be ashamed to.
try: Say this dua once today: Rabbana innana amanna faghfir lana dhunubana.

title: Five habits, ending in the quiet before dawn.
subtitle: What the mindful actually do

key.label: The last third of the night

then: Ibn Kathir lists these qualities and highlights the last. In the hadith, {reward}every night in the last third, Allah asks who is seeking forgiveness so He may forgive.{/reward} He notes Ibn Umar would ask if the late night had come, then pray until dawn.
now: You wake at 4am for no reason and reach for your phone. {idea}That might be the best hour of your day.{/idea} A minute of asking forgiveness while the house is silent.
old: The middle of the night is wasted time.
new: The pre-dawn quiet is when Allah is asking who wants forgiveness.
try: Set an alarm 10 minutes before Fajr once this week and say astaghfirullah.

title: Allah testifies first, then the angels, then the people of knowledge.
subtitle: The greatest testimony, and who gets to join it
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is the most truthful and just witness, and He named the angels and the people of knowledge alongside His testimony. {reward}This shows the great virtue of those who have knowledge.{/reward} He also {idea}maintains His creation in justice{/idea} in all He does.
now: You keep meaning to take that class or finally read a tafsir. Life is busy. {reward}The verse places people of knowledge in a line with the angels.{/reward} Each thing you learn about Allah makes you a better witness.
old: Learning about my faith is something for scholars.
new: Knowing Allah well lets me stand with the witnesses to His oneness.
try: Learn the meaning of one of Allah's names today, and use it in a dua.

title: They split after knowledge came, out of rivalry.
subtitle: The true religion, and why people divide over truth
then: Ibn Kathir explains that submission to Allah, following all His messengers, is the religion with Him. Those given scripture before divided {trap}out of envy, hatred and enmity{/trap}, after proofs had come. {trap}Hatred made some reject the other side even when it was right.{/trap}
now: Your cousin makes a good point in the family argument and you refuse to admit it because it is him. {trap}That is the same disease.{/trap} Disagreements often come from rivalry, not from missing facts.
old: I would never reject a truth I clearly know.
new: Envy can make me refuse what I know is right, just because of who said it.
try: Admit someone you dislike was right about one thing, out loud or in your heart.

title: Your job is to convey, not to convince.
subtitle: When someone argues about your faith
then: Ibn Kathir explains that when people argued about Allah's oneness, the Prophet ﷺ was told to say he had made his worship sincere for Allah. {idea}If they turned away, his duty was only to convey.{/idea} Their reckoning is with Allah, who knows who deserves guidance.
now: Your friend asks about Islam, then pushes back hard. You leave feeling you failed because they did not agree. {reward}You did your part.{/reward} Guidance is not in your hands.
old: If they do not accept, I failed.
new: My part is to share clearly and kindly. The heart is in Allah's hands.
try: Make dua by name for someone you once tried to explain Islam to.

title: Silencing the one who calls for justice.
subtitle: Arrogance that rejects the truth and its messengers
then: Ibn Kathir explains this censures those among the People of the Book who denied Allah's signs and {trap}killed prophets who only called them to the truth{/trap}, and people who ordered justice. He cites the hadith: arrogance is refusing the truth and degrading people.
now: In a meeting, someone points out a fair problem with your plan. You roll your eyes and talk over them. {trap}That small move is the seed of what this verse describes.{/trap} {idea}The fix is listening when someone calls for fairness.{/idea}
old: Arrogance is about bragging, and I do not brag.
new: Arrogance is refusing truth and dismissing people, even quietly.
try: The next time someone corrects you today, thank them before you answer.

title: Their deeds came to nothing, here and after.
subtitle: When good works are emptied out
then: This continues the previous verse about those who rejected the truth and harmed its callers. Ibn Kathir notes they were punished with {trap}humiliation in this life and loss in the Hereafter{/trap}, their works lost and with no helpers.
now: You give, volunteer, help out, then hold it over people. Or you do good while refusing to hear any correction. {idea}Good deeds need a humble heart to carry them.{/idea}
old: As long as I do good things, it all counts.
new: Arrogance can empty out my deeds, so I guard my heart as well as my actions.
try: Do one good deed today and tell no one, not even as a hint.

title: Invited to their own book, they turned away.
subtitle: Following scripture only when it agrees with you

row.title: me
sub: I follow it when I like it

then: Ibn Kathir explains that those who claimed to follow the Torah and the Gospel were called to refer to them, books which commanded them to follow the Prophet ﷺ. {trap}When called, a group turned away with aversion.{/trap}
now: You quote verses when they win you the argument with your spouse. When one cuts against you, you change the subject. {idea}The Book is either the judge or it is not.{/idea}
old: I follow the Quran, as long as it does not cost me much.
new: I let the Book judge me too, not only the people I argue with.
try: Think of one dispute you are in. Ask honestly what the Quran says, even if it goes against you.

title: Just a few days in the Fire, they told themselves.
subtitle: The comfortable lie that makes wrongdoing easy
then: Ibn Kathir explains what made them dare to defy the truth was a claim that {trap}the Fire would only touch them for a few days{/trap}. They deceived themselves with it, though Allah gave no authority for that claim.
now: It is only a small lie. Allah is forgiving anyway. I will repent later. {trap}These are the phrases you hear in your own head right before you do it.{/trap} {idea}Hope is real, but not as a license.{/idea}
old: Allah is forgiving, so this small thing does not matter.
new: Hoping for mercy is right, but using it as an excuse is self-deception.
try: Catch one excuse you tell yourself today and say the honest version instead.

title: Every soul paid in full, and no one wronged.
subtitle: The Day that ends all self-deception
then: After their comfortable claim, Allah asks how it will be when He gathers them on the Day about which there is no doubt. Ibn Kathir explains {idea}each person will be paid in full what he earned{/idea}, and none will be dealt with unjustly.
now: You worked late and your colleague took the credit. {reward}On that Day, nothing is misplaced.{/reward} {idea}And your own quiet wrongs are on the same scale.{/idea} Full justice is good news and a reminder at once.
old: What I do quietly will just disappear.
new: Every deed is kept and paid in full, fairly, mine included.
try: Fix one small wrong you did this week, before that Day does it for you.

title: Power is given and taken. It was never yours to keep.
subtitle: A prayer to the Owner of all sovereignty
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say this while praising and trusting his Lord. Ibn Kathir says it encourages {reward}gratitude for the favors granted to him and his community{/reward}, and refutes those who thought they could decide for Allah who deserves His message.
now: You got the promotion. Or the title went to someone else. {idea}Either way, it passed through His hand first.{/idea} That makes the win humble and the loss bearable.
old: My position is something I built and own.
new: Every bit of power or honor I hold is on loan from the Owner.
try: Thank Allah today for one position you hold: parent, manager, elder sibling.

title: Night into day, living from dead. Turning is His habit.
subtitle: The One who turns things around, every day

row.title: it will always be this way

then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah lengthens one and shortens the other through the seasons. He brings {idea}the plant from the seed and the seed from the plant, the faithful from the disbeliever{/idea}, and provides for whom He wills out of wisdom and justice.
now: Winter evenings swallow the afternoon, then summer gives it back. The son who gave up praying starts again. {reward}The account that was empty fills.{/reward} {idea}Nothing you see stays fixed in His hands.{/idea}
old: My situation is stuck, and nothing will change.
new: The One who turns night into day turns situations too.
try: Watch one sunrise or sunset this week and ask Allah to turn one hard thing.

title: Whose side are you on when it counts?
subtitle: Loyalty, and the warning that Allah sees it
then: In Madinah, the young Muslim community faced pressure from many sides. Ibn Kathir explains the verse forbids {trap}taking the enemies of faith as close supporters instead of the believers{/trap}, with an exception for someone who fears for their safety. {idea}Allah warns of Himself, and to Him is the return.{/idea}
now: Your friends mock a fellow Muslim in the group chat, and laughing along keeps you in the circle. {idea}The question is quiet: where does your heart sit when it costs something?{/idea}
old: I go along with whoever keeps me comfortable.
new: My deepest loyalty belongs to Allah, and He knows where my heart leans.
try: Next time someone is mocked for their faith around you, say one kind word for them.

title: Hidden or shown, your heart is known.
subtitle: What you hold inside is not private from Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah's knowledge covers all secret and apparent matters, {idea}not even the weight of an atom escapes Him{/idea}. The verse alerts people to fear Him enough to avoid what He dislikes, since He knows all and is able over all.
now: You smile at your in-law while holding a grudge. You give in the masjid while hoping someone notices. {idea}What you carry inside is as visible to Him as your face.{/idea}
old: As long as I act right, what I feel inside is my business.
new: My heart is open to Allah, so I work on it as much as my actions.
try: Before one good deed today, pause and fix your intention for Allah alone.

title: He warns you because He is kind.
subtitle: Every deed waiting, and a warning that is mercy
then: Ibn Kathir explains every soul will find its good and evil brought before it. Seeing the good brings joy; seeing the evil, one wishes for a great distance from it. Then comes hope: {reward}Al-Hasan Al-Basri said Allah is so kind that He warns them against Himself.{/reward}
now: A good doctor tells you your blood test is bad before it is too late. {reward}That warning is the kindest thing she could do.{/reward} {idea}You still have time to put distance between you and what you regret.{/idea}
old: Warnings about the Day just make me anxious.
new: The warning is mercy, given while I can still change things.
try: Pick one habit you would want far from you on that Day, and take a step away from it.

title: Love Allah? Follow the Prophet, and Allah will love you.
subtitle: The test of a claim to love
then: Ibn Kathir says Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others among the early Muslims explained that {idea}some people claimed to love Allah, so Allah tested them with this verse{/idea}. Ibn Kathir adds that {reward}what they earn is greater than what they sought: Allah's love for them.{/reward}
now: You post a beautiful quote about loving Allah. Then the day goes by without one sunnah. {idea}Love shows in what you copy.{/idea} A smile, a dua before eating, a gentle word.
old: I love Allah in my heart, and that is enough.
new: Love for Allah shows in following His Messenger, and it is answered with His love.
try: Pick one small sunnah you do not do yet and do it today.

title: Obey Allah and the Messenger. That is the whole instruction.
subtitle: A simple command and what turning away means
then: Right after the test of love, the command is put plainly. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}defying the Messenger's way while claiming to love Allah{/trap} is not accepted, and that Allah does not like those who turn away.
now: You know the instruction. The excuse forms quickly: not now, too busy, the situation is different. {idea}The verse is short because the thing is simple.{/idea}
old: I will obey once life is less complicated.
new: Obedience is the simple proof of love, today, in small steps.
try: Do one thing today you know Allah asked of you that you have been delaying.

title: Allah chose Adam, Nuh, and two families.
subtitle: The chosen ones, and the family this surah is named after
then: This opens the part of the surah linked by Maududi to the delegation from Najran. Ibn Kathir explains Allah honored Adam, made Nuh the first messenger, who {idea}called his people day and night for a very long time{/idea}, and chose the families of Ibrahim and Imran, the father of Maryam.
now: You wonder if your life matters in the big story. The chosen ones were not chosen for comfort. {idea}They were chosen to carry something.{/idea} Your own small trust, a child, a parent, a job done well, is part of that line.
old: Being chosen by Allah means things will be easy.
new: Being chosen is a trust to carry, and every believer carries some of it.
try: Read or listen to the story of Nuh in the Quran this week.

title: One family line, passing faith down.
subtitle: Descendants, some from others
then: The chosen families were {idea}descendants, one from the other{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes that Isa came from the offspring of Ibrahim. Allah, All-Hearing and All-Knowing, knew who would carry the trust in each generation.
now: Your kid watches you pray, or watches you skip it. Your niece hears how you talk about your parents. {reward}Faith runs down family lines through small, daily things.{/reward}
old: What I pass on to my kids is mostly money and opportunities.
new: The most lasting thing I pass on is my faith, shown more than said.
try: Let a child in your family see you make dua today, and tell them what you asked for.

title: She gave her unborn child to Allah.
subtitle: A mother's vow before she knew who she carried
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Ishaq that she could not have children, and {idea}seeing a bird feed its chick, she prayed for a child{/idea}. When she knew she was pregnant, she vowed the child to the worship and service of the masjid in Jerusalem.
now: You hold the ultrasound photo, or the baby is asleep on your chest. {reward}The first prayer you make over them shapes what you want for them.{/reward} Success, yes. But also: Allah, let them be Yours.
old: My children are mine to plan for.
new: My children are a trust I can offer back to Allah.
try: Make one dua tonight for a child in your life to be close to Allah.

title: She expected a son. Allah knew better.
subtitle: The birth of Maryam and a mother's protection
then: She had expected a male for service in the masjid. Yet {idea}Allah knew better what she bore.{/idea} She named her Maryam and sought refuge for her and her offspring from Shaytan. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that {reward}Maryam and her son were not touched by Shaytan at birth.{/reward}
now: The plan did not go your way: a different child, a different job, a different city. {idea}Allah knew better what you were given.{/idea} The mother of Maryam did not argue. She protected what she got.
old: This is not what I asked for, so it is a setback.
new: Allah knows better what He gave me, so I care for it and seek His protection.
try: Say a dua of protection over someone you love today, by name.

title: Where is this from? From Allah.
subtitle: Maryam's provision and Zakariyya's question
then: Allah accepted Maryam and made her grow well, placing her with Zakariyya so she could learn from him. Many early scholars said {reward}he found summer fruit with her in winter and winter fruit in summer.{/reward} Her answer was simple: it is from Allah.
now: A refund arrives the week rent is due. A neighbor drops off food when the fridge is empty. {idea}You ask: where did that come from?{/idea} Maryam already gave the answer.
old: Everything I have comes from my own hard work.
new: My effort matters, but every provision is from Allah.
try: When something good arrives today, say out loud: this is from Allah.

title: He saw a miracle, and it made him ask for one.
subtitle: Zakariyya's prayer in old age
then: Ibn Kathir explains that when Zakariyya saw Allah provide for Maryam out of season, {idea}he became eager for a child of his own{/idea}. He was old with grey hair, and his wife was barren. Still, he called on Allah in secret.
now: Your friend's prayer gets answered: the visa, the baby, the cure. A quiet voice says yours is too far gone. {idea}Zakariyya let someone else's miracle make him braver, not jealous.{/idea}
old: Some things are too late for me to even ask for.
new: If Allah gives out of season for others, I can ask Him too.
try: Make dua today for the one thing you stopped asking for.

title: The answer came while he was still praying.
subtitle: Glad tidings of Yahya
then: The angels called him while he stood in prayer. Ibn Kathir notes the name Yahya means he lives, since {reward}Allah filled his life with faith{/reward}. Many early scholars said he would believe in Isa, the Word from Allah. The news that he would be a prophet was better still.
now: You ask for a job and get a job with people who make you better. You ask for a child and get a child who teaches you patience. {reward}Allah's answers often come bigger than the request.{/reward}
old: If I get exactly what I asked for, I will be happy.
new: Allah can answer with more than I knew to ask for.
try: Stay in your prayer place for one extra minute after salah today and make dua.

title: How? Allah does what He wills.
subtitle: When the good news sounds impossible
then: Hearing the good news, Zakariyya wondered how it could happen at his age with a barren wife. Ibn Kathir explains the reply: {idea}this is Allah's matter, He is so mighty that nothing escapes His power.{/idea}
now: The doctor gave you the numbers. The bank said no. Your mind keeps listing the reasons it cannot happen. {idea}It is fine to ask how.{/idea} {reward}Just remember who you are asking.{/reward}
old: The facts say it cannot happen, so it will not.
new: Facts bind me, not Allah. He does what He wills.
try: Write down one thing you think is impossible, and under it write: Allah does what He wills.

title: Three days of silence, filled with remembrance.
subtitle: The sign given to Zakariyya
then: Zakariyya asked for a sign that the child was coming. Ibn Kathir explains he would {idea}not be able to speak except by signals, though he was not mute{/idea}. And he was told to remember his Lord much and glorify Him morning and evening.
now: You lose your voice, or your phone breaks, or you are stuck in a waiting room for hours. {reward}A forced pause can be the best time for dhikr.{/reward} Zakariyya could not talk to people, but he could talk to Allah.
old: When I cannot do my usual things, the time is lost.
new: A quiet stretch is a chance to remember Allah more.
try: Spend five minutes in silence today saying subhanAllah, with your phone in another room.

title: Chosen, purified, and chosen again.
subtitle: The angels speak to Maryam
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah chose Maryam {idea}because of her service to Him, her modesty, honor, and conviction{/idea}. He cites the hadith that the best woman of her time was Maryam, and of the Prophet's ﷺ time, Khadijah.
now: Nobody at work notices your quiet prayers in the stairwell. Nobody tags you for keeping your dignity. {reward}Maryam was chosen above the women of the worlds for exactly that kind of hidden devotion.{/reward}
old: Quiet devotion does not get noticed.
new: Allah notices and honors the hidden service of His servants.
try: Do one act of worship today that only Allah will see.

title: Honored? Then pray more.
subtitle: What Maryam was told to do with her honor
then: Right after telling her she was chosen, the angels told her to worship more. Ibn Kathir explains this was so she could carry {idea}what Allah had decreed for her as a test{/idea}, a son without a father, which earned her a higher grade in this life and the next.
now: You got the good news: the acceptance letter, the engagement, the new role. {idea}That is exactly when you need more prayer, not less.{/idea} Blessings come with tests attached.
old: When things go well, I can ease off worship.
new: Honor and blessing are reasons to bow lower and pray more.
try: After your next piece of good news, pray two extra rakat of thanks.

title: You were not there. Allah told you.
subtitle: The lots cast for Maryam's care
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Ikrimah and others that the scholars of the masjid each wanted to care for Maryam, seeking reward. {idea}They threw their pens into the river{/idea}, and only Zakariyya's stayed in place. The Prophet ﷺ was not there; Allah revealed it to him.
now: Think of the people who once competed to do good for you: the aunt who wanted to raise you, the teacher who stayed late. {reward}Being cared for is its own blessing.{/reward} {idea}So is competing to care for others.{/idea}
old: People only compete for money and positions.
new: The best people compete to take care of others, for Allah's reward.
try: Volunteer for one caring task today before anyone else claims it.

title: A Word from Allah, named the Messiah, son of Mary.
subtitle: The good news of Isa
then: Ibn Kathir explains Isa came into being with a word from Allah: Be. He was called the Messiah because {reward}those he touched were healed by Allah's leave{/reward}, and named after his mother because {idea}he had no father{/idea}. He would be honored and among those near to Allah.
now: Your Christian neighbor asks what Muslims believe about Jesus. You might be surprised how much you can say. {reward}He is honored, near to Allah, a Word from Him.{/reward} He also has a mother whose name he carries.
old: Isa belongs to another religion's story.
new: Isa is honored in my own faith, a servant brought near to Allah.
try: Learn one thing the Quran says about Isa, so you can share it kindly if asked.

title: A baby speaks, and a man speaks the same message.
subtitle: Isa in the cradle and in maturity
then: Ibn Kathir explains Isa called to the worship of Allah alone {idea}while still in the cradle, as a miracle{/idea}, and again as a man by revelation. He cites the hadith that only a few infants ever spoke in the cradle, Isa among them. He would be one of the righteous.
now: At twenty you were sure of your faith. At forty, the job and the mortgage blur it. {idea}Isa's message as a baby and as a man was the same.{/idea} Your core can stay steady while your life changes.
old: Faith naturally changes as I get older and busier.
new: My circumstances change, but what I call to can stay the same.
try: Recall what first made you feel close to Allah, and do that thing once this week.

title: Be, and it is.
subtitle: Maryam's question and Allah's answer
then: Maryam asked how she could have a son when no man had touched her. Ibn Kathir notes the angel said Allah {idea}creates{/idea}, rather than does as with Zakariyya, to remove any doubt about Isa. {reward}What Allah wills comes into existence instantly.{/reward}
now: You have a plan with fourteen steps and you are stuck on step two. {idea}Your steps matter, but they are not the limit.{/idea} The One you pray to does not need steps.
old: Things can only happen the normal way, one step at a time.
new: When Allah decrees something, He says Be, and it is.
try: Bring your hardest problem to Allah in dua today, without explaining how He should solve it.

title: He would be taught writing, wisdom, Torah and Gospel.
subtitle: What Allah would teach Isa
then: Ibn Kathir says the good news to Maryam was even greater because {reward}Allah would teach Isa writing and wisdom{/reward}, and both the Torah and the Gospel. He notes Isa memorized both books.
now: You read something that finally makes sense, or a skill clicks after months of practice. {idea}Every bit of knowledge is taught.{/idea} Even a prophet's learning came from Allah.
old: What I know, I figured out myself.
new: Whatever I learn is taught to me by Allah.
try: Before you study or read today, say: Rabbi zidni ilma, my Lord, increase me in knowledge.

title: Every miracle came with the words: by Allah's permission.
subtitle: The signs of Isa
then: Ibn Kathir notes scholars said every prophet got a miracle suited to his time. Musa came when magic was prized; {idea}Isa came when medicine was advancing{/idea}, and no physician could do what he did. Each sign was {reward}by Allah's leave{/reward}, proof of who sent him.
now: Your surgery goes well and you thank the surgeon. You should. {idea}And you can remember the permission behind it.{/idea} Even Isa repeated it, every time.
old: Talented people make good things happen on their own.
new: Every skill and success works by Allah's permission.
try: When you thank someone today, also say alhamdulillah in your heart.

title: He came to confirm, and to ease some burdens.
subtitle: Isa's mission to the Children of Israel
then: Ibn Kathir explains Isa affirmed the Torah and {reward}made lawful part of what had been forbidden{/reward}, clearing up some of their disputes. He then said, as the next verse continues, that {idea}Allah is my Lord and your Lord{/idea}, equal in servitude to Him.
now: A good teacher does not want you to worship them. They point past themselves. {idea}Isa said obey me so that you would worship Allah.{/idea} The test of any guide is where they point you.
old: Following a good teacher means putting them on a pedestal.
new: The best guides point beyond themselves to Allah.
try: Thank a teacher who pointed you toward Allah, by message or in a dua.

title: My Lord and your Lord. That is the straight path.
subtitle: Isa's own summary of his message
then: This closes Isa's words to the Children of Israel. Ibn Kathir explains the meaning: {idea}I and you are equal in our servitude, submission and humbleness to Him.{/idea} Worshipping Allah alone is the straight path.
now: You meet someone whose faith is deeper than yours and feel small. Or someone looks up to you and you feel big. {idea}In front of Allah, everyone is a servant on the same path.{/idea}
old: Very holy people are on a different level from the rest of us.
new: From prophets to me, we are all servants of the same Lord.
try: In your next sujood, say quietly: my Lord, and the Lord of everyone I know.

title: Who will help me for Allah? A few stepped forward.
subtitle: The disciples answer Isa's call
then: When Isa sensed they were set on disbelief, he asked who would help him convey Allah's message. Ibn Kathir compares it to the Prophet ﷺ asking at Hajj who would shelter him, {reward}until he found the Ansar{/reward}. Hawari means supporter, and the Prophet ﷺ called Az-Zubayr his.
now: The masjid asks for volunteers. The group chat goes quiet. Everyone waits for someone else. {reward}The disciples were the ones who said: us.{/reward}
old: Someone else will step up. They always do.
new: When the call for help comes, I can be the one who answers.
try: Answer one request for help this week that you would usually let pass.

title: Write us down among the witnesses.
subtitle: The disciples' prayer
then: The disciples did not stop at words. They declared belief, said they followed the messenger, and asked to be counted. Ibn Kathir reports that Ibn Abbas explained the witnesses here as {reward}the community of Muhammad ﷺ{/reward}.
now: You sign up for the thing, show up, help clean up after. Nobody posts about it. {reward}The disciples asked to be written down by Allah, not noticed by people.{/reward}
old: If no one sees my effort, it was for nothing.
new: I want my name written with Allah, whoever else sees it.
try: Say the disciples' prayer today: Rabbana amanna bima anzalta wattaba'na ar-rasul.

title: They planned. Allah planned. His plan won.
subtitle: The plot against Isa
then: Ibn Kathir describes how they {trap}spread lies about Isa and complained to the king{/trap}, who sent men to capture him. Allah raised Isa up and saved him, leaving them thinking they had succeeded.
now: Someone at work is building a case against you with half-truths. You lie awake running scenarios. {idea}You are not the only one with a plan here.{/idea} Do what is right and let the best Planner handle the rest.
old: If people plot against me, I am finished.
new: Allah is the best of planners, and His plan has the last word.
try: Hand one worry about someone's scheming to Allah in dua tonight, then sleep.

title: Raised to Allah, and every dispute returns to Him.
subtitle: Allah's promise to Isa
then: Ibn Kathir reports Al-Hasan said take you refers to sleep, as {idea}Allah raised Isa while he was asleep{/idea}. After he was raised, people split over him. {idea}All will return to Allah, who will judge what they disputed.{/idea}
now: Every night you sleep and wake. The Prophet ﷺ would say on waking: praise be to Allah who gave us life after death. {reward}That small return is a preview.{/reward} {idea}Every argument you lose sleep over will be settled by Him.{/idea}
old: I have to win every argument about faith right now.
new: Allah will judge every difference. My job is to hold the truth well.
try: When you wake tomorrow, say: Alhamdulillahi alladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana.

title: No helpers, here or after.
subtitle: The end of those who rejected
then: Continuing Allah's words to Isa, this verse sets out what awaits those who rejected after the signs came. {trap}Severe punishment in this world and the next{/trap}, and no one to help them.
now: You rely on your circle, your family name, your lawyer cousin. {idea}They help here, sometimes.{/idea} This verse turns your attention to the only help that reaches everywhere, and asks what you are doing to keep it.
old: My people will always have my back.
new: The only help that never fails is Allah's, so I hold on to Him.
try: Ask Allah today to be your helper, in your own words, in one sentence.

title: Believe and do good. Every reward, paid in full.
subtitle: The other side of the promise
then: After the warning comes the promise. Those who believed and did righteous deeds {reward}will be given their rewards in full{/reward}. And Allah does not like the wrongdoers.
now: You helped your mother with paperwork for three hours. Nobody said thank you. {reward}It is counted, in full.{/reward} Not a minute is lost when faith is behind it.
old: A lot of my good deeds just disappear unnoticed.
new: Every good deed done with faith is paid back in full.
try: Do one good deed today that has been waiting on your list.

title: This story is a wise reminder, recited to you.
subtitle: Why these accounts are told
then: After telling of Maryam, Zakariyya, Yahya and Isa, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ {idea}this is what We recite to you of the verses and the wise reminder{/idea}. The surah's opening section, Ibn Kathir notes, was sent in reply to the questions brought about Isa.
now: You scroll past a Quran story because you have heard it before. {idea}Stories are told to change something in you, not to inform you once.{/idea} Each time you meet Maryam, ask what she is showing you today.
old: I already know these stories.
new: The stories are reminders, and I need reminding again and again.
try: Reread the story of Maryam in this surah and pick one line for yourself.

title: Isa is like Adam. Both began with Be.
subtitle: The answer to the Najran delegation
then: Ibn Kathir reports that {idea}a delegation of Christians from Najran came to Madinah to argue that Isa was divine{/idea}, and the opening of this surah came in reply. If no father made Isa divine, then {idea}Adam, with no father or mother, would be more so{/idea}, which is clearly false.
now: Someone asks you a hard question about your faith and your mind goes blank. {reward}The Quran answers with a calm comparison, not insults.{/reward} One clear point, made gently, is worth more than a heated thread.
old: Hard questions about faith are something to avoid.
new: The truth can be explained calmly, with one clear comparison.
try: Learn this verse's argument well enough to explain it in two sentences.

title: The truth is from your Lord. Do not doubt.
subtitle: Settling the heart after the argument
then: After the comparison with Adam, the verse closes the matter. Ibn Kathir explains {idea}this is the only true story about Isa{/idea}, and what is beyond the truth except falsehood?
now: You watch a video arguing against your faith at 1am, and it nags at you all week. {idea}Doubt grows when you forget the source.{/idea} The truth you hold did not come from a debate, so a debate does not undo it.
old: Every clever argument I hear shakes my faith.
new: The truth is from my Lord, so I can listen without being uprooted.
try: When a doubt comes up, write it down and look up the answer from a trusted source this week.

title: Bring your families, and let Allah judge who is lying.
subtitle: The challenge of the Mubahalah
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Ishaq that the Najran delegation argued about Isa until this verse came. The Prophet ﷺ called them to the Mubahalah. {idea}They asked for time, conferred, and declined{/idea}, choosing instead to make a treaty and return home.
now: You claim something in the family argument. Your aunt says: swear by Allah. {trap}Suddenly you are less sure.{/trap} {idea}Before you insist, ask if you would put your name on it before Allah.{/idea}
old: I can be loud about things I am only half sure of.
new: I only insist on what I would stand behind before Allah.
try: Before your next strong claim, ask yourself: would I swear by Allah on this?

title: This is the true account. There is no god but Allah.
subtitle: The conclusion of the story of Isa
then: After the challenge, the verse states the outcome plainly. As Ibn Kathir said of the story of Isa, {idea}this is the only true story, and what is beyond the truth save falsehood?{/idea} It ends where every prophet's message ends: there is no god but Allah.
now: Your feed has five versions of every event, each sure of itself. {idea}When it comes to Allah, you are not left guessing.{/idea} The Quran tells the story and names it true.
old: Everyone has their own version, and none is final.
new: Allah has told me the true account, and I can rest on it.
try: Say la ilaha illallah slowly ten times today, thinking about each word.

title: If they turn away, Allah knows.
subtitle: Leaving the outcome with Allah
then: The challenge had been made and the truth set out. If they still turned away, there was nothing left to force. {idea}Allah knows those who spread corruption.{/idea} The matter rests with Him.
now: You explained, you were patient, you were fair. They still walked away angry. {reward}You do not have to have the last word.{/reward} {idea}Allah sees the whole thing.{/idea}
old: If they walk away, I have to go after them and win.
new: Once I have said the truth fairly, I can let Allah handle the rest.
try: Let one argument go today without sending the last message.

title: Come to a word that is fair between us.
subtitle: Common ground, offered to the People of the Book
then: Ibn Kathir explains this is a fair word for both sides, the message of all messengers. Ibn Jurayj said not taking each other as lords means {idea}we do not obey each other in disobedience to Allah{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ quoted this verse in his letter to Heraclius.
now: Your boss asks you to fudge the numbers. Your friend wants you to follow them into something wrong. {idea}Taking someone as a lord can look like simply obeying them over Allah.{/idea}
old: If someone important tells me to, I go along with it.
new: No person's command comes before Allah's, however important they are.
try: Notice one person whose approval you chase more than Allah's, and pray about it.

title: Ibrahim came before the Torah and the Gospel.
subtitle: An argument that falls apart on the timeline
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Abbas that {idea}the Christians of Najran and Jewish rabbis argued before the Prophet ﷺ{/idea}, each claiming Ibrahim as theirs. The verse points out both scriptures came after him.
now: Two cousins argue over which side of the family grandpa liked more. Neither was born when he made his choices. {idea}Sometimes the simplest fact ends the argument.{/idea}
old: The great people of the past were on my side.
new: I check the facts before claiming the righteous as my own.
try: Before your next argument, check one basic fact first.

title: Why argue about what you do not know?
subtitle: The limit of a fair debate
then: Ibn Kathir says the verse criticizes those who {trap}argue and dispute without knowledge{/trap}. They were told to refer what they did not know to Allah, who knows the seen and unseen and the true reality of all things.
now: Someone in the comments asks a deep question about the unseen. Ten people with no background answer at once. {idea}I don't know is an honest answer, and Allah knows is a better one.{/idea}
old: If I don't have an answer, I'll look weak.
new: Saying I do not know, and Allah knows, is honest and safe.
try: Say I don't know once today when you truly do not, without guessing.

title: Ibrahim belonged to no label but submission.
subtitle: Who Ibrahim really was
then: Ibn Kathir explains Ibrahim was {idea}a true Muslim, hanif, shunning shirk and living in faith{/idea}, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah. Labels came later; his devotion came first.
now: You say you are Muslim on a form. Your neighbor says she is from a religious family. {idea}Ibrahim is defined by what he did with his heart.{/idea} The label matters less than the turning.
old: Being born into the right group is what counts.
new: What counts is a heart that turns to Allah alone, like Ibrahim's.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: what is one thing I worship besides Allah without noticing?

title: Closest to Ibrahim are the ones who follow him.
subtitle: Belonging is earned by following
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that every prophet had a close one among the prophets, and {reward}the Prophet's ﷺ was his father Ibrahim, the intimate friend of Allah{/reward}. Those most worthy of Ibrahim are those who follow his way.
now: You come from a family of scholars, or a family that never prayed. {idea}Neither decides how close you are.{/idea} Closeness to Ibrahim is about following, and anyone can start today.
old: My family background decides how religious I can be.
new: Anyone who follows Ibrahim's way is close to him, whatever their family.
try: Learn one dua of Ibrahim from the Quran and use it today.

title: Those who try to mislead only mislead themselves.
subtitle: The harm that comes back to the one who causes it
then: In Madinah, some among the People of the Book wished they could pull the believers away from their faith. Ibn Kathir notes {trap}the punishment of this behavior falls back on them, while they are unaware{/trap}.
now: You are tempted to quietly turn a friend against someone you dislike. {trap}The damage starts in your own heart first.{/trap} {idea}And if someone does it to you, stay steady; it is not yours to carry.{/idea}
old: If I steer others wrong, it only affects them.
new: Trying to mislead others harms my own soul first.
try: If you have been nudging someone away from a good thing, stop today.

title: Why deny what you yourself bear witness to?
subtitle: Knowing the truth and still refusing it
then: Ibn Kathir explains the question: {trap}you know for certain that Allah's verses are true and authentic{/trap}, so why reject them? The issue was not missing knowledge but refusing what they already saw.
now: You know you should call your father. You know the habit is hurting you. {idea}Most of the time the gap is not knowledge, it is acceptance.{/idea} The verse asks the same question of you.
old: If I really knew, I would change.
new: I often already know. The question is whether I will act.
try: Pick one thing you already know you should do and do it today.

title: Mixing truth with falsehood, while knowing better.
subtitle: Blending a lie into something true

row.title: falsehood
sub: so no one can separate them

row.title: concealing
sub: is its own wrong when you know

then: Some of the People of the Scripture in Madinah knew from their own books the description of the Prophet ﷺ. Instead of saying so, they {trap}blurred the truth with falsehood and hid what they knew{/trap}. The verse asks them plainly: why?
now: A work report where the numbers are true but the one bad figure is buried in a footnote. A story to your parents that is ninety percent accurate. {trap}The half-truth is harder to catch than the lie.{/trap} {idea}You know which part you left out.{/idea}
old: If every sentence I said was technically true, I was honest.
new: Honesty is judged by what I knew and chose to hide, not only by what I said.
try: Think of one half-told story you gave someone this week. Fill in the missing part.

title: Believe at dawn, reject by dusk, to shake others.
subtitle: A plan to make faith look broken
then: A faction planned to join the dawn prayer with the Muslims and then reject Islam by evening. The aim was that people weak in faith would think, {trap}they must have found something wrong in it{/trap}. It was theatre meant to unsettle.
now: Someone you respected posts a long thread about why they stopped praying. A cousin says religion did nothing for them. You feel the floor move. {idea}Another person's exit is not evidence.{/idea} The truth was true before they arrived and after they left.
old: If people who knew it leave, maybe there is something wrong with it.
new: Who walks in or out does not change what is true. I check the source, not the crowd.
try: When a doubt comes from someone's exit, write down the actual claim and look into that claim alone.

title: Guidance and bounty are in Allah's hand, not ours.
subtitle: Hoarding knowledge to stay ahead of others

row.title: no one equals us
sub: or argues with us before Allah

row.title: Allah gives
sub: to whom He wills, without limit

then: They told one another not to share their knowledge with the Muslims, so the Muslims would not become their equals or use it as proof against them. The reply: {idea}true guidance is Allah's guidance{/idea}, and {reward}all bounty is in His hand{/reward}.
now: You know the shortcut at work that saves hours, and you keep it to yourself so you stay the one people need. A classmate asks for your notes and you say you lost them. {trap}Holding it close feels like safety.{/trap} {idea}Your place was never yours to guard.{/idea}
old: If I teach others what I know, I lose my advantage.
new: What I have came from Allah's hand, and sharing it cannot shrink His giving.
try: Share one useful thing you know with a colleague or friend today, with no strings.

title: He chooses for His mercy whom He wills.
subtitle: Mercy is not a family inheritance
then: This closes the reply to those who thought guidance belonged only to their own people. Ibn Kathir explains that Allah {reward}honored the believers with a great favor{/reward}, sending them the final Prophet ﷺ. {idea}The gift was His to give.{/idea}
now: You grew up in a practicing family and quietly assume you are fine. Or you grew up far from faith and assume you never will be. {trap}Both are the same mistake.{/trap} {reward}His mercy is wider than your background.{/reward}
old: Where I come from decides how close I can be to Allah.
new: Mercy is chosen and given by Allah, so I ask for it, not assume it or give up on it.
try: Ask Allah by name for His mercy today, in your own words, as if for the first time.

title: Some return a fortune, some keep a single coin.
subtitle: Honesty that changes depending on who you deal with

row.title: one coin
sub: kept unless you stand over him

then: The verse is fair: among the People of the Scripture were people you could trust with a fortune. Others would not return a coin, saying {trap}there is no blame on us in taking from the unlettered{/trap}. Ibn Kathir notes Ibn Abbas told some Muslims who reasoned the same way that {idea}this is exactly what the People of the Book said{/idea}.
now: You would never cheat a friend, but padding an expense claim at a big company feels fine. Or skipping the fare because the operator is faceless. {trap}A different rule for people outside my circle.{/trap} {idea}Honesty does not check membership.{/idea}
old: Cheating someone who is not one of us does not really count.
new: My honesty is owed to everyone, and calling it permitted is a lie about Allah.
try: Return or settle one small thing you have been keeping because the owner seemed too big or too distant to matter.

title: Keep your word and fear Allah, and He loves you.
subtitle: The real answer to the coin excuse
then: After the excuse of the coin, the verse answers: {idea}Yes, there is blame.{/idea} Whoever keeps his pledge and fears Allah is loved by Him. Ibn Kathir links the pledge to the covenant to believe in the final Messenger ﷺ when he came.
now: You told the landlord you would pay on the first. You told your kid you would come to the game. No one would sue you for missing it. {reward}Keeping it anyway is what Allah loves.{/reward}
old: A promise only matters if someone can hold me to it.
new: A kept promise, with Allah in mind, is a way to be loved by Him.
try: Keep one small promise today exactly as you said it, on time.

title: Selling your oath for a small price costs everything.
subtitle: The false oath that wins a small gain

row.title: no share
sub: no word, no look, no purifying

then: Ibn Kathir records that al-Ash'ath said this verse came down about him, in a dispute over land where the other side could win by simply taking an oath. Another man, told {reward}Paradise{/reward} was the reward for giving up a claim, said: {idea}bear witness that I give up all the land{/idea}.
now: "I swear it was like this when I got it." Said at a returns desk, to an insurance agent, in a family inheritance fight. {trap}One sentence, and the thing is yours.{/trap} The price is always smaller than it looks.
old: A small lie under oath is worth it to win what is mine anyway.
new: No gain is worth trading my word to Allah, and losing it with honesty is still winning.
try: Before you say "I swear" today, stop and check that every word is true.

title: Twisting your tongue so it sounds like Scripture.
subtitle: Presenting your own words as Allah's

row.title: their own words
sub: said in the tone of Scripture

then: A party would recite with a twist of the tongue, adding or bending meanings so listeners thought it was from the Book. Ibn Kathir explains they {trap}altered the meanings and attributed their own words to Allah{/trap}, knowing they lied.
now: In a family argument you say "Islam says" when you mean "I think." A forwarded message in the group chat with a hadith no one has checked. {trap}Borrowing Allah's authority for your own point.{/trap} {idea}Say plainly which part is yours.{/idea}
old: If it supports something good, it is fine to say the religion says it.
new: Putting my words in Allah's mouth is a lie about Him, even for a good cause.
try: Next time you quote religion in an argument, check the source first or say "I think" instead.

title: No prophet says worship me. He says be people of the Lord.
subtitle: Knowledge should point beyond the one who teaches it
then: No one given the Book, wisdom, and prophethood would tell people to worship him. Ibn Kathir says the criticism is aimed at {trap}teachers of misguidance{/trap}. A prophet would say: be Rabbaniyyun, which Ibn Abbas explained as {idea}wise, learned, and forbearing{/idea}, because you teach and study the Book.
now: You follow a speaker online and start defending him harder than you defend the Quran. Or people come to you for advice and you enjoy being needed a little too much. {idea}A good teacher makes you need him less.{/idea}
old: The more people rely on me, the better I am doing my job.
new: Real knowledge points people to Allah, not to the person who carries it.
try: When you teach or advise someone today, point them to the source so they can go back without you.

title: No prophet asks you to take angels or prophets as lords.
subtitle: Respect is not worship
then: The verse completes the thought: a prophet would never order people to take angels or prophets as lords. Ibn Kathir cites that {idea}every messenger was sent with: worship Me alone{/idea}. Calling to anything else would be {trap}calling to disbelief after submission{/trap}.
now: You love a scholar, a saint, a teacher who changed your life. That love is good. {trap}It becomes a problem when their word outranks His.{/trap} {idea}The best of them would be the first to say so.{/idea}
old: Loving a righteous person deeply means giving their word the final say.
new: The righteous I love would want me to put Allah above them, and so do I.
try: Think of someone you admire in faith. Ask what they would want you to put first, and do that.

title: Every prophet pledged to support the Messenger to come.
subtitle: A covenant Allah Himself witnessed

row.title: support the truth
sub: even when it comes after you

then: Allah took a pledge from the prophets: whatever Book and wisdom He gave them, if a messenger came confirming it, they would believe in him and help him. Ali and Ibn Abbas said {idea}every prophet pledged this about Muhammad ﷺ{/idea}. Allah said: {reward}bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses{/reward}.
now: You built the project at work, and now a newer colleague arrives with a better plan that fits your own work. Your rank says defend your turf. {idea}The pledge says help the truth, whoever carries it.{/idea}
old: What I already have is enough. I don't need to make room for what comes after.
new: Even prophets were asked to support the truth that came after them. Rank serves truth.
try: Openly back one good idea today that came from someone junior or newer than you.

title: Turning away after the pledge is rebellion.
subtitle: Breaking a promise you already said yes to
then: Right after the covenant, the verse says whoever turns away from it after that {trap}is among the defiantly disobedient{/trap}. Ibn Kathir explains it as turning from {idea}fulfilling the pledge and covenant{/idea} that had been confirmed and witnessed.
now: Ramadan ends and the resolutions from the last ten nights quietly fade. You said yes to Allah in sujood, crying. {trap}Then life went back to normal.{/trap} {idea}The yes still stands. You can return to it.{/idea}
old: Promises I made in an emotional moment don't really bind me.
new: A yes I gave Allah is a pledge. Walking away from it is the real danger.
try: Recall one promise you made to Allah in a hard moment. Do one small part of it today.

title: Everything already submits. Will you choose to?
subtitle: Willing or unwilling, all returns to Him
then: The verse asks those who wanted another way: is it other than Allah's religion you want? Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}the believer submits in heart and body{/idea}, while the one who refuses {trap}submits in body only{/trap}, because no one escapes His control.
now: Your heart beats without asking you. You fall asleep whether you planned to or not. Gravity holds your coffee cup in place. {idea}You already live inside His order.{/idea} {reward}The only choice left is whether your heart joins in.{/reward}
old: Submitting to Allah means giving up my freedom.
new: I am already held by His order. Choosing to submit is joining willingly what I cannot escape.
try: Notice three things in your body today that happen without your permission. Thank Allah for each.

title: We believe in all the prophets, without distinction.
subtitle: One message from Ibrahim to Muhammad ﷺ
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to declare faith in Allah and in what came to Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, the tribes, Musa, Isa and all the prophets. Ibn Kathir: {idea}Muslims believe in every prophet and every Book Allah sent{/idea}, and {trap}never disbelieve in any of them{/trap}.
now: You read the story of Musa ﷺ as if it belongs to someone else's history. Or Isa ﷺ feels like another religion's figure. {idea}They are your prophets too.{/idea} Their stories are your inheritance.
old: The earlier prophets belong to other people. Mine is only Muhammad ﷺ.
new: Every prophet is part of my faith, and their lessons are written to me as well.
try: Read or listen to one short story of a prophet other than Muhammad ﷺ today and take one lesson from it.

title: A way other than submission will not be accepted.
subtitle: What counts is the way Allah set
then: This follows the declaration of faith in all prophets. Ibn Kathir explains it as {trap}whoever seeks other than what Allah legislated{/trap}, and cites the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}whoever does a deed not in line with our matter, it is rejected{/idea}.
now: You build a little custom religion: keep the parts you like, skip the parts that cost you. A prayer here, a holiday there. {trap}It feels personal and sincere.{/trap} {idea}Sincerity still needs the right shape.{/idea}
old: As long as I mean well, the form of my worship doesn't matter.
new: Meaning well matters, and so does doing it the way Allah asked.
try: Pick one act of worship you do by habit and check today how the Prophet ﷺ actually did it.

title: Turning away after seeing the clear signs.
subtitle: When the proof was already in your hands
then: Ibn Abbas reported that a man of the Ansar accepted Islam, then left and joined the idolaters. {idea}He later regretted it{/idea} and sent his people to ask if he could repent. These verses came down, through to {reward}Allah is Forgiving, Merciful{/reward}, and he returned.
now: You saw an answered dua. You felt peace in a prayer you can still remember. Then a busy year, a new circle, and it all feels distant. {trap}Forgetting what you once saw clearly.{/trap} The man in this story still came back.
old: What I felt back then was just a phase.
new: The signs I once saw were real. Walking away from them is the danger, and the way back is still open.
try: Write down one moment you clearly felt Allah's help. Keep it where you will see it.

title: Their reward is distance from all mercy.
subtitle: The outcome of turning away after knowing
then: The verse describes the outcome for those of the previous verse who {trap}turned away after clear signs{/trap}. The curse means being far from mercy. The next verses keep the door open: {reward}except those who repent{/reward}.
now: You keep putting off coming back, as if there is always next month. The verse is sober about where that road ends. {idea}It is a warning given early, while you can still turn.{/idea}
old: Consequences are far away. There is no rush.
new: A warning is a mercy when it comes in time to change direction.
try: Name one thing you have been putting off returning to Allah about. Take the first small step today.

title: No lightening, no delay, once the time has passed.
subtitle: Why now is the time to turn

row.title: now
sub: while it can still be changed

then: This continues the description of those who left the faith after clear proof and stayed away. Ibn Kathir says {trap}the torment will not be lessened, not even for an hour{/trap}. Then comes the exception in the very next verse: {reward}those who repent{/reward}.
now: Deadlines at work get extended. Bills can be paid late with a fee. You are used to life giving you one more chance. {idea}Today is the extension.{/idea}
old: There is always more time to make things right.
new: There is a last day for turning back, and today is still before it.
try: Make one sincere istighfar today, in your own words, for something specific.

title: Except those who repent and set things right.
subtitle: The door that stays open
then: After the warnings comes one word: except. This is the verse the man from the Ansar heard. Ibn Kathir calls it a sign of {reward}Allah's kindness, compassion and mercy{/reward} toward those who {idea}repent to Him{/idea}.
now: You left prayer for years. You said things about faith you regret. You think the door shut behind you. {reward}Read the word "except" again.{/reward} {idea}Turn back, then repair one thing.{/idea}
old: After what I did, there is no way back for me.
new: Repentance plus repair is always met by a Forgiving, Merciful Lord.
try: Repent sincerely for one thing, then do one concrete act that sets it right.

title: Repentance at the very end is not accepted.
subtitle: Leaving again and again until death
then: Ibn Abbas reported some people accepted Islam, left, returned, and left again. Ibn Kathir explains the verse is about those who {trap}insist until death{/trap}, linking it to {idea}repentance being of no effect when death is already present{/idea}.
now: "I'll get serious when I'm older." You say it at twenty, then at forty. A phone call from a hospital reminds you that no one gets a schedule. {idea}Repentance works best while it still feels early.{/idea}
old: I can always turn back at the end.
new: Turning back is a gift of the living. I don't get to choose my last day.
try: Do the thing you planned to do "when you are older" in its smallest form today.

title: An earth full of gold could not ransom them.
subtitle: What could have been given, cheaply, in life
then: Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: a man is asked whether he would ransom himself with the earth's fill of gold, and he says yes. He is told {idea}I asked you for what is less and easier than that{/idea}. He was also asked about a generous man, and said it did not help because {trap}he never once asked, Lord, forgive my sins{/trap}.
now: You give to charity, help neighbors, show up for people. All good. But you have never once sat down and said, "My Lord, forgive me." {idea}What Allah asks is small, and it is asked now.{/idea}
old: If I do enough good, I won't need to turn to Allah.
new: Good deeds need a heart turned to Allah. What He asks is much less than gold.
try: Say "Rabbi ighfir li khati'ati yawm ad-din" (my Lord, forgive my sins on the Day of Judgment) once today, meaning it.

title: You won't reach righteousness until you give what you love.
subtitle: Giving the best, not the leftovers
then: Abu Talhah owned a garden facing the Prophet's mosque ﷺ, where the Prophet ﷺ would drink its water. Hearing this verse he gave it away. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}that is profitable wealth{/reward} and advised giving it to his relatives. Umar asked the same about {idea}his most precious land in Khaybar{/idea}.
now: Clearing out the closet for the donation bin, you give the jacket you never wear. The one you love stays on the hanger. {idea}Righteousness lives in the second one.{/idea} {reward}It is not loss. It is profit.{/reward}
old: Giving what I don't need is still generous.
new: The giving that reaches righteousness is the giving that costs me something I love.
try: Give one thing today that you actually like, not just what you can spare.

title: Bring the Torah and read it, if you are truthful.
subtitle: Settling a dispute by going to the source

row.title: Israel's vow
sub: camel meat and milk, in illness

then: Some claimed laws had never changed. Ibn Kathir records that the Prophet ﷺ reminded them Israel (Ya'qub) {idea}vowed during a long illness to give up his favorite food and drink{/idea}, and they agreed. The verse invites them: {reward}bring the Torah and recite it{/reward}.
now: A family argument about what grandfather really said in his will. A heated thread about what a study proved. Everyone is sure. {idea}Go get the document and read it together.{/idea}
old: Whoever argues the most confidently must be right.
new: The fair way to settle a claim is to open the source and read it honestly.
try: In your next disagreement, suggest checking the original source together before arguing further.

title: Inventing lies about Allah after the proof is wrongdoing.
subtitle: When the evidence is in and you still insist
then: After the call to bring the Torah, the verse says whoever still {trap}invents a lie about Allah{/trap} is the wrongdoer. Ibn Kathir explains it as those who claimed Allah would never send another prophet, {idea}though evidence showed laws had changed before{/idea}.
now: You checked. The source says you were wrong. Now comes the moment where you could say "I see" or find a new angle to keep your position. {idea}Saying "I was wrong" is the honest exit.{/idea}
old: Admitting I was wrong makes me look weak.
new: Holding on after the proof is clear turns a mistake into wrongdoing.
try: Admit one thing you were wrong about recently, out loud, to the person involved.

title: Allah has spoken the truth. Follow Ibrahim's upright way.
subtitle: Back to the shared root
then: After the debate, the Prophet ﷺ is told to say: {idea}Allah has spoken the truth{/idea}, so follow the religion of Ibrahim. Ibn Kathir calls it {reward}the straight, complete and clear way{/reward}, and cites other verses that say the same.
now: You spent an hour arguing about religion online and haven't prayed yet. You know every counterpoint and none of the practice. {idea}The argument ends. The way begins.{/idea}
old: Knowing I'm right is the main thing.
new: Truth is meant to be followed, the way Ibrahim followed it, not just defended.
try: After your next religious discussion, go and do one act of worship before anything else.

title: The first House set up for people was at Bakkah.
subtitle: Where worship on earth began
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Ka'bah was built by Ibrahim, whose religion others claimed. The Prophet ﷺ was asked which mosque came first and said {idea}al-Masjid al-Haram, then al-Aqsa, forty years later{/idea}. He added: {reward}wherever prayer time finds you, pray, for the whole earth is a mosque{/reward}.
now: You may never have seen the Ka'bah except on a screen, yet you turn toward it five times a day from a bedroom, an office, a parking lot. {idea}The first House is the center of your direction.{/idea}
old: Makkah is far away, something for one trip in my life.
new: I face the first House every day. The blessing it holds reaches me through every prayer.
try: At your next prayer, pause before takbir and picture the House you are facing.

title: Clear signs, safety, and a journey owed to Allah.
subtitle: The House that invites whoever can reach it
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the Maqam is the stone Ibrahim stood on to raise the walls while {idea}Isma'il handed him the stones{/idea}, and Mujahid said his footprints remain on it. Even before Islam, a man in fear {reward}was safe inside the Haram{/reward}.
now: You have a savings jar labeled "Hajj someday" that keeps getting borrowed from. Or you have already been and the memory is fading. {idea}The invitation stands.{/idea} {reward}Allah needs nothing from it. You do.{/reward}
old: Hajj is a duty for later, when life is settled.
new: The House is an invitation to safety and nearness, meant for me while I am able.
try: If you have not been, write down one real step toward Hajj. If you have, make dua for someone who longs to go.

title: Why reject the signs while Allah is Witness?
subtitle: Knowing, refusing, and being seen
then: Ibn Kathir notes that earlier prophets had {reward}brought good news of the coming Prophet ﷺ{/reward}. Those who knew this still {trap}rejected him{/trap}. Allah reminds them that He witnesses all they do.
now: You read the verse, you know it applies to you, and you scroll past. No one in the room noticed. {idea}Someone did.{/idea}
old: If no one sees me ignore what I know, it doesn't matter.
new: Allah witnesses what I do with what I know, even in a quiet room.
try: Act on one thing you already know you should do, today, simply because He sees.

title: Why block others from the path and make it look crooked?
subtitle: Turning people away from good

row.title: "it's crooked"
sub: while they knew it was straight

then: The verse continues the address: why {trap}turn the believers away from Allah's path{/trap}, trying to make it seem crooked, while you are witnesses? Ibn Kathir says they {idea}knew what the Messenger ﷺ brought was the truth{/idea}.
now: Your friend starts praying again and you joke, "Here comes the sheikh." Your sibling wears hijab for the first time and you ask if she is sure. {trap}A small laugh can push someone off a path.{/trap} {idea}Be the one who makes it easier.{/idea}
old: I'm only joking. It's their choice anyway.
new: My words can make the straight path look crooked to someone. I want them to make it look beautiful.
try: Encourage one person today who is trying to come closer to Allah.

title: Obey the wrong voices and they will turn you back.
subtitle: Who you take direction from
then: The believers are warned that obeying a party who {trap}envy them for the favor Allah gave{/trap} would lead them back to disbelief. Ibn Kathir links it to another verse about those who wished the believers would turn away {idea}out of their own envy{/idea}.
now: The influencer you watch daily slowly shapes what you think is normal, what is cringe, what is old-fashioned. You never decided to follow him. {trap}You just kept obeying the feed.{/trap} {idea}Notice who is steering.{/idea}
old: What I watch and listen to doesn't change what I believe.
new: Whoever I keep obeying, even passively, slowly becomes my guide.
try: Look at the three accounts you watch most. Ask honestly where each is steering you.

title: How could you disbelieve with the verses right here?
subtitle: Holding firmly to Allah

row.title: those after
sub: who found only pages and believed

then: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith: the Prophet ﷺ asked whose faith is most amazing. Not the angels, not the prophets, not the Companions, he said, but {reward}people after you who find only written pages and believe in them{/reward}. And {idea}whoever holds firmly to Allah is guided{/idea}.
now: You never saw the Prophet ﷺ. You have a mushaf on a shelf and an app on your phone. {reward}That is the faith he called amazing.{/reward} The verses are still here, recited to you.
old: Faith was easier for people who lived with the Prophet ﷺ.
new: Believing through the pages alone is the faith the Prophet ﷺ admired, and the verses are still with me.
try: Open the Quran today and read one page slowly, as if it were being recited to you.

title: Fear Allah as He deserves, and die only in submission.
subtitle: Living the way you hope to end

row.title: a last-minute fix
sub: I'll sort it at the end

then: Ibn Mas'ud explained taqwa as Allah's due: {idea}obeyed and not defied, remembered and not forgotten, thanked and not unthanked{/idea}. Ibn Kathir adds that a person dies upon how they lived. Three nights before he died, the Prophet ﷺ said {reward}die only thinking well of Allah{/reward}.
now: Monday morning, inbox open, you forgot Allah until lunch. Payday, you forgot to say alhamdulillah. {idea}Taqwa is remembering in those exact moments.{/idea} {reward}And through it all, think well of Him.{/reward}
old: As long as I'm right with Allah at the end, I'm fine.
new: I end the way I live, so I keep Him remembered and thanked now, and think well of Him.
try: Set three moments today, waking, lunch, bed, to remember and thank Allah in one sentence.

title: Hold Allah's rope together. He turned enemies into brothers.
