subtitle: Unity as a gift to remember
then: Ibn Kathir says this came about the Aws and Khazraj of Madinah, who had {trap}fought long wars with great hatred{/trap}. Islam made them {reward}brothers who loved each other{/reward}. At Hunayn the Prophet ﷺ reminded them: were you not divided, and Allah united you?
now: The cousins who haven't spoken since the wedding. The mosque committee split over the parking lot. {trap}Old wounds kept open.{/trap} {idea}Remember who joined you in the first place.{/idea}
old: Some divisions are too deep to heal. It's just how families are.
new: Allah has joined hearts that hated each other for generations. Holding His rope together is the way.
try: Send one warm message today to someone you have drifted from or quarrelled with.

title: Let there be people who call to good and stop wrong.
subtitle: Doing your part in changing what's wrong
then: Ibn Kathir explains a group should take this task, yet it is {idea}on every member, each by ability{/idea}. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: whoever sees a wrong, change it {reward}with the hand, then the tongue, then the heart{/reward}.
now: In the office group chat someone shares a cruel joke about a coworker. Everyone sends a laughing emoji. You could stay silent, or type "not cool." {idea}Start where your ability reaches.{/idea}
old: Calling to good is the scholars' job, not mine.
new: Everyone has a share in this, starting with whatever my hand, tongue or heart can do.
try: Next time something wrong happens in front of you, do the smallest kind thing that pushes back.

title: Don't split apart after the clear proofs arrive.
subtitle: Division that follows clarity
then: Ibn Kathir says the believers are forbidden from {trap}imitating the division and discord of earlier nations{/trap}, who also abandoned enjoining good. Mu'awiyah, on Hajj, warned that if they did not {idea}hold to what came from their Prophet ﷺ{/idea}, others would hold to it even less.
now: The argument at the mosque about which way to do something minor turns into two groups that stop greeting each other. {trap}Same Book, same Prophet ﷺ, two camps.{/trap} {idea}Disagree without splitting.{/idea}
old: If I'm right on this point, it's fine to break off from those who aren't.
new: Splitting after clear guidance is the warning itself. Unity is part of following the proof.
try: Greet warmly today someone you disagree with on a religious point.

title: On that Day, some faces brighten and some darken.
subtitle: What shows on your face at the end
then: Ibn Abbas said bright faces belong to {reward}those of the Sunnah and the community{/reward}, dark ones to those of innovation and division. Al-Hasan said the dark-faced who are asked {trap}did you disbelieve after your belief{/trap} are the hypocrites.
now: You catch your face in a dark phone screen after an hour of gossip. Or you see it glow at the end of a long night prayer. {idea}Faces carry what you did.{/idea}
old: What I do privately doesn't show on me.
new: On that Day my deeds will show on my face. I want it to carry light.
try: Do one quiet good deed today that no one will see, hoping it brightens your face that Day.

title: Bright faces live inside Allah's mercy, forever.
subtitle: The end the verses are pointing you toward
then: After the warning, the verse turns to {reward}those whose faces will be bright{/reward}. Ibn Kathir explains they are in Allah's mercy, Paradise, {idea}where they will never desire to be moved{/idea}.
now: You come home after a long trip, drop your bag, and feel that sigh: home. Now imagine a home you never want to leave, and the verse calls it {reward}mercy{/reward}.
old: Paradise is a reward I have to fully earn on my own.
new: Paradise is called Allah's mercy. I work for it and I hope in it.
try: Ask Allah for His mercy and Paradise today, by name, after one of your prayers.

title: These verses are recited in truth. Allah wants no injustice.
subtitle: The warnings come from a just Lord

row.title: truth
sub: the real picture of both worlds

row.title: to be harsh
sub: to scare for its own sake

then: After describing bright and dark faces, Allah says these verses are recited {reward}in truth{/reward}. Ibn Kathir explains He is the Just Ruler who {idea}never treats His creatures with injustice{/idea}, needing nothing from anyone.
now: A doctor who tells you the hard truth about your blood test is not being cruel. She wants you well. {idea}The warnings you just read are like that.{/idea}
old: Warnings about the Day make Allah sound harsh.
new: The warnings come from a Lord who wants no injustice for me. They are the truth told in time.
try: Reread one warning verse today and ask what it is protecting you from.

title: Everything belongs to Allah, and every matter returns to Him.
subtitle: Who has the final say

row.title: His decision
sub: in this life and the next

then: This closes the passage on unity and the Day of bright and dark faces. Ibn Kathir: all are {idea}His servants and His property{/idea}, and {reward}His is the decision{/reward} in this life and the Hereafter.
now: You are waiting on the visa decision, the job offer, the test result. It feels like everything depends on one office. {idea}That office belongs to Him too.{/idea}
old: My future is in the hands of the people deciding my case.
new: Every matter, including the one I am waiting on, returns to Allah.
try: For the decision you are waiting on, make dua first, then follow up.

title: The best community, on one condition: good, wrong, and faith.
subtitle: A title that comes with a job

row.title: by the condition
sub: whoever fulfills it shares the praise

then: Ibn Kathir explains it as {reward}the best of peoples for the people{/reward}, the most beneficial to mankind. Umar recited this on Hajj, seeing the crowds, and said {idea}whoever wants to be of this community, let him fulfill Allah's condition{/idea}.
now: You say "we're the best ummah" in a heated comment thread. Then you scroll past someone being mocked and say nothing. {idea}The title is a job description.{/idea}
old: Being Muslim makes me part of the best community automatically.
new: The best community is the one that does good, stops wrong and believes. I earn my share by doing it.
try: Do one thing today that is useful to someone outside your own circle.

title: They can annoy you, but they cannot truly harm you.
subtitle: Hostility that hurts but cannot break

row.title: a trifling annoyance
sub: the verse's own size for it

then: The early believers in Madinah faced open hostility. Ibn Kathir calls this verse {reward}good news to the believers{/reward}: opponents would bring {trap}only a trifling annoyance{/trap}, and would not be helped against them.
now: The coworker who undermines you in meetings. The relative who mocks your prayer. It stings every time. {idea}Allah calls it annoyance, not ruin.{/idea}
old: Their hostility can wreck my life.
new: People can annoy me, but they cannot touch what Allah protects.
try: Next time someone needles you for your faith, respond calmly once, then let it go.

title: Small disobedience, repeated, grew into rejecting the signs.
subtitle: How great wrongs begin
then: The verse describes humiliation that came upon those it addresses, except under a covenant from Allah and from people. It names the cause twice. Ibn Kathir explains that what led them to {trap}reject Allah's signs and kill His messengers{/trap} was that {idea}they often disobeyed and crossed His limits{/idea}.
now: Skipping one prayer becomes skipping the day. One white lie at work becomes the way you handle every awkward question. {trap}Nobody falls far in one step.{/trap} {idea}Watch the small repeat.{/idea}
old: Little sins are harmless. I'd never do anything serious.
new: Repeated small disobedience is how hearts get ready for big wrongs.
try: Pick one small sin you repeat often. Break the streak once today.

title: They are not all the same.
subtitle: Never judging a whole group by some

picture.label: Among the People of the Book

then: Right after strong criticism, the Quran says: {idea}they are not all alike{/idea}. Ibn Kathir reports it came about scholars of the People of the Book who believed, like Abdullah bin Salam. They {reward}stood at night reciting Allah's verses in prostration{/reward}.
now: A bad experience with one person from a certain background and you start saying "those people." A news story and suddenly a whole group has one face. {idea}Even after criticism, the Quran stops to be fair.{/idea}
old: Once I've seen the worst of a group, I know what they're all like.
new: Allah Himself says they are not all the same. I owe people that fairness too.
try: Catch yourself once today saying "they all" about any group, and correct it.

title: They believe, call to good, and race toward good deeds.
subtitle: Hastening, not just doing

row.title: believe
sub: in Allah and the Last Day

then: The verse continues the praise of those among the People of the Book who believed. Ibn Kathir notes they {idea}implement the Book and follow the Prophet ﷺ{/idea}, and they {reward}hasten in all good works{/reward}.
now: A fundraiser link in the group chat. You think, I'll donate later. Later never comes. {reward}Righteous people click first.{/reward}
old: Good deeds can wait until I have more time.
new: Righteousness is a pace. The righteous hurry to good.
try: Do the next good deed that crosses your path today immediately, without postponing.

title: No good they do will be denied them.
subtitle: Nothing good is lost with Allah
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}their good deeds will not be lost with Allah{/reward}, for {idea}no deed escapes His knowledge{/idea}, nor is any reward for doing good ever lost with Him.
now: You stayed late to clean up after the event and no one noticed. You cared for a parent for years and siblings never said thanks. {reward}It is not lost.{/reward}
old: If no one notices the good I do, it's as if it didn't happen.
new: Allah knows every good deed, and none of it is thrown away.
try: Do one good thing today and deliberately tell no one about it.

title: Wealth and children will not shield anyone from Allah.
subtitle: What can't stand between you and Him
then: After praising the upright, the verse turns to those who disbelieve: {trap}neither wealth nor children will avail them against Allah{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says {idea}nothing can avert His punishment{/idea} for them.
now: The life insurance, the property, the kids who will be successful. You feel safe because of them. {idea}They are gifts for here.{/idea} Before Allah, only faith and deeds stand.
old: With enough money and a good family, I'm secure.
new: Nothing I own or raised can stand in for faith before Allah.
try: Use some of your money or time today for something that will count with Allah.

title: Spending without faith is a harvest hit by frost.
subtitle: Building on a foundation that cannot hold
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the wind of sir is {trap}a freezing wind that burns crops like fire{/trap}, striking produce ready to harvest and depriving its owner {idea}when he needs it most{/idea}. Such spending was not built on firm foundations.
now: Months of work on a project, then the hard drive dies with no backup. That sinking feeling. {idea}Make sure your good deeds are backed up with faith and sincerity.{/idea}
old: Any good I do will count, whatever my intention.
new: Good deeds need the foundation of faith and sincerity, or the harvest can be lost.
try: Before your next act of giving, pause and make your intention for Allah alone.

title: Don't make insiders of those who wish you harm.
subtitle: Choosing who sits in your inner circle
then: Ibn Kathir explains the warning was against taking as close advisors {trap}those who wished the believers hardship{/trap}, who had access to their secrets. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: every leader has {idea}two circles of advisors, one urging good and one urging evil{/idea}.
now: The friend who always knows your business and somehow your business always gets around. The colleague whose advice keeps landing you in trouble. {idea}Ask who your inner circle actually wants for you.{/idea}
old: Anyone who is nice to me can be trusted with everything.
new: My inner circle should be people who want good for me and urge me toward it.
try: Think of who you share your private worries with. Ask if they push you toward good.

title: You love them, they don't love you back.
subtitle: Two faces: kind in public, enraged in private
then: The believers liked certain hypocrites, thinking they were believers. Ibn Kathir: they {trap}pretended kindness in public and concealed rage in private{/trap}. The verse ends: {idea}Allah knows what is in the hearts{/idea}.
now: Now turn it on yourself. You are warm to someone's face, then roll your eyes in the group chat after. {trap}Two faces is easy to slip into.{/trap} {idea}Allah sees the private one.{/idea}
old: What I say about people in private doesn't matter if I'm nice to their face.
new: Allah knows what is in my heart. I want my private face to match my public one.
try: Say nothing about someone today that you wouldn't say to their face.

title: Patience and taqwa make their plots harmless.
subtitle: The defense that works
then: Ibn Kathir notes when the believers had good years they were displeased, and when hardship came, {trap}as at Uhud{/trap}, they were pleased. Allah's direction: {idea}be patient and fear Allah{/idea}, and {reward}their cunning will not harm you at all{/reward}.
now: The rival who smirks when you fail and goes quiet when you succeed. You want to beat them at their game. {idea}The verse offers a different plan: patience and taqwa.{/idea} Allah surrounds what they do.
old: I have to scheme back to protect myself from people who want me to fail.
new: Patience and fearing Allah are the real protection. He surrounds whatever they do.
try: When someone's envy bothers you today, answer with sabr and a quiet dua instead of a counter-move.

title: He left home at dawn to place each believer at his post.
subtitle: The morning of Uhud, and a Lord who hears

row.title: hold your station
sub: the archers were told: do not leave

then: After Badr, Quraysh marched on Madinah with three thousand. The Prophet ﷺ consulted, put on his armor, and went out. He placed fifty archers on a hill and told them {idea}stay in your positions, win or lose{/idea}. Allah {reward}heard what was said and knew what hearts concealed{/reward}.
now: Your post may be the night shift, the carpool, the parent who stays home with a sick kid while everyone else goes to the event. It feels small. {idea}Someone placed you there for a reason. Hold it.{/idea}
old: My role is too small to matter in the bigger picture.
new: Every post matters, and Allah hears and knows how I hold mine.
try: Do your most ordinary responsibility today with full care, as if it were your station.

title: Two groups nearly lost heart, but Allah was their protector.
subtitle: Wavering is not the end of the story
then: On the way to Uhud, Abdullah bin Ubayy turned back with a third of the army. Two clans {trap}were about to lose heart{/trap}. Jabir, from one of them, said he would not wish the verse unrevealed, because it says {reward}Allah was their protector{/reward}.
now: You almost quit the course. You nearly walked out of the marriage counselling session. Your nerve failed for a moment. {reward}Allah stayed your ally in that moment too.{/reward} {idea}Lean on Him and keep going.{/idea}
old: Because I wavered, Allah must be disappointed with me.
new: Even when my courage shakes, Allah remains my protector. I put my trust in Him and continue.
try: In the thing you nearly gave up on, take one more step today and say hasbiyallah.

title: Allah gave you victory at Badr when you were few.
subtitle: Remembering past help in a hard moment

row.title: Allah alone
sub: so fear Him and be grateful

then: In the middle of the Uhud passage, Allah reminds them of Badr. Ibn Kathir: the Muslims were {idea}three hundred and thirteen, with two horses and seventy camels{/idea}, against a far larger, better-equipped army. The lesson: {reward}victory is only from Allah{/reward}.
now: You are facing a new hardship and feel small. Scroll back in your own memory: the exam you thought you'd fail, the month rent seemed impossible. {reward}He helped you then.{/reward}
old: This time I don't have enough to get through.
new: Allah helped me when I had little before. Gratitude for that is my strength now.
try: Write down one past "Badr" in your life, a time Allah carried you through with little.

title: Is it not enough that your Lord sends three thousand angels?
subtitle: Reassurance when the news is bad
then: Scholars differ whether this refers to Badr or Uhud. Ash-Sha'bi reported that at Badr the Muslims heard {trap}a chief was coming to reinforce the idolaters{/trap}, and it weighed on them. The Prophet ﷺ was told to say: {reward}is it not enough that your Lord reinforces you with three thousand angels?{/reward}
now: The rumor at work: layoffs coming. The message from the landlord: rent going up. Your mind adds up everything against you. {idea}Add what you cannot see.{/idea}
old: I can only count on what I can see and measure.
new: Allah's help is real even when it's unseen. Is it not enough?
try: When bad news comes today, before reacting, ask: is my Lord not enough?

title: Be patient and mindful, and help will come in force.
subtitle: Help that comes with a condition
then: Ibn Kathir notes that on the view that this refers to Uhud, {trap}the angels did not come there{/trap}, because the help was conditional on patience and taqwa, and some left their posts. Ali said that at Badr {reward}the angels were marked with white wool{/reward}.
now: You prayed for help with your finances, then kept spending the same way. You asked for calm, then reached for the argument. {idea}The promise is real, and so is the "if".{/idea}
old: If I ask for Allah's help, it should come regardless of what I do.
new: Allah's help is promised to the patient and mindful. My part is to meet the condition.
try: In one situation you're asking Allah to help with, do your part of the "if" today.

title: The angels were good news. Victory comes from Allah alone.
subtitle: Means that reassure, a Source that decides
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah sent the angels and told them about it {reward}to encourage and reassure their hearts{/reward}, and so they would know {idea}victory only comes from Allah{/idea}, who could defeat any enemy without them.
now: The good doctor, the strong lawyer, the generous relative. Thank them. But when the scan comes back clear, {idea}remember who decided it{/idea}.
old: Things worked out because I found the right people.
new: The right people were Allah's comfort to me. The outcome was His.
try: Thank one person who helped you recently, and then thank Allah for sending them.

title: So their plans to harm would end in frustration.
subtitle: Wrong aims that come back empty
then: This verse continues the reasons for Allah's help in battle. Ibn Kathir explains that those who came {trap}to harm the believers{/trap} would {idea}return to their land frustrated, without achieving their aims{/idea}.
now: Turn it inward. When you set out to hurt someone with words, to win at any cost, to get even, how often did you come back empty and bitter? {idea}Harmful aims tend to end that way.{/idea}
old: If I push hard enough, I'll get the result I want.
new: An aim to harm ends in frustration. I want my aims to be ones Allah can bless.
try: Drop one plan to get even with someone today.

title: The decision is not yours. He may forgive them yet.
subtitle: Even the worst may later be guided
then: Ibn Kathir reports the Prophet ﷺ, wounded at Uhud, said {trap}how can a people succeed who did this to their Prophet{/trap}, and supplicated against certain leaders. This verse came. Several of those named {reward}were later pardoned after they accepted Islam{/reward}.
now: The relative who hurt you, the colleague who sabotaged you. You've decided who they are forever. {idea}That decision is not yours.{/idea} You can protect yourself and still leave the door open for them.
old: Some people will never change. I know how their story ends.
new: Allah decides people's endings. Some I wrote off may be guided before me.
try: Make a short dua for guidance for one person you have written off.

title: He forgives whom He wills. And He is Forgiving, Merciful.
subtitle: The verse ends on forgiveness
then: After telling the Prophet ﷺ the decision is not his, Allah says all belongs to Him. Ibn Kathir: {idea}His is the decision and none can resist it{/idea}. And the verse closes: {reward}Allah is Forgiving, Merciful{/reward}.
now: Lying awake replaying what you did. You fear you're on the wrong side of "whom He wills." {reward}Read how He chose to end the sentence.{/reward}
old: Allah's power over me is something to fear only.
new: His power is total, and He describes Himself, right then, as Forgiving and Merciful.
try: Say "Ya Ghafur, ya Rahim" today and ask for forgiveness for one specific thing.

title: Don't feed on interest that doubles and multiplies.
subtitle: Profiting from someone who cannot pay
then: Between the passages on Uhud comes a different battle. Ibn Kathir describes the pre-Islamic practice: when a loan fell due the lender said {trap}pay now or it grows{/trap}, year after year, until a small sum was multiplied. The believers are told to fear Allah {reward}that they may succeed{/reward}.
now: Your cousin asks for a loan and you start thinking about what you'll get back on top. Or you watch a friend drown in a debt that keeps growing. {idea}The verse points to a different kind of success.{/idea}
old: Money lent should always make me more money.
new: Real success comes from fearing Allah, not from profiting off someone's hardship.
try: If someone owes you, consider giving them more time or easing it a little.

title: Guard yourself from the Fire prepared for the disbelievers.
subtitle: A warning placed right after the loan verse

row.title: guard yourself
sub: in how you deal and earn

row.title: dealings matter
sub: warned of in the same breath

then: Ibn Kathir notes that after forbidding multiplied interest, Allah {trap}warns them against the Fire{/trap} and commands them to {idea}obey Allah and the Messenger that they may obtain mercy{/idea}. The warning sits right beside a money matter.
now: You think of the Hereafter in the mosque, not at the checkout, not in the contract, not in the loan you're about to sign. {idea}The Quran puts them in the same paragraph.{/idea}
old: How I handle money is separate from my faith.
new: My dealings with money are part of what protects me from the Fire, or exposes me to it.
try: Before your next financial decision, pause and ask if Allah would be pleased with it.

title: Obey Allah and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.
subtitle: Obedience as the path to mercy
then: After the warning comes the way out. Ibn Kathir pairs this verse with the previous one: {trap}fear the Fire{/trap}, and {reward}obey Allah and the Messenger that you may obtain mercy{/reward}.
now: Your alarm for Fajr goes off and obedience feels like a cost. Then you stand in the quiet and something settles. {reward}That calm is mercy coming through the door you opened.{/reward}
old: Obeying is something I do for Allah, and it costs me.
new: Obeying is how I place myself where His mercy falls.
try: Do one act of obedience today you've been delaying, and notice how you feel afterward.

title: Hurry to forgiveness and a Garden as wide as heavens and earth.
subtitle: Hurry, there is room

row.title: life is short
sub: the room is endless, the time is not

then: Ibn Kathir notes Allah {idea}encourages rushing to good deeds{/idea}, and the width points to Paradise's vastness. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: when you ask for Paradise, {reward}ask for al-Firdaws, the highest{/reward}.
now: You hurry for a sale that ends at midnight, the last train, a concert ticket drop. {idea}Bring that urgency here.{/idea} The Garden is wide; your days are not.
old: There's always time to get serious about Paradise later.
new: Paradise has endless room, but my time to hurry toward it is limited.
try: When you make dua today, ask Allah for al-Firdaws by name.

title: They give in ease and hardship, swallow anger, and pardon.
subtitle: Three marks of the people of the Garden

row.title: they hold anger
sub: though able to act on it

then: Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}the strong one is he who controls himself when angry{/reward}. And {idea}no gulp is dearer to Allah than a gulp of anger a servant swallows{/idea}, which fills him with faith.
now: Someone cuts you off in traffic. Your teenager slams the door. Your boss blames you in front of everyone. {idea}The gulp is right there.{/idea} Swallow it, then let it go.
old: If I don't react, people will walk all over me.
new: Holding back anger and pardoning is strength Allah loves, not weakness.
try: The next time anger rises today, wait ten seconds before answering, and forgive one small thing.

title: When they slip, they remember Allah and ask forgiveness.
subtitle: The people of the Garden also sin
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith: a man sins and says {idea}Lord, I sinned, forgive me{/idea}, and Allah says {reward}My servant knew he has a Lord who forgives; I have forgiven him{/reward}. It repeats again and again. Anas was told that when this verse came, Iblis wept.
now: Same sin, third time this month. The voice says: stop pretending, you're a hypocrite. {reward}That voice is not Allah's.{/reward} {idea}Remember Him, ask again, and stop where you can.{/idea}
old: If I keep falling into the same sin, my repentance is fake.
new: Every return counts. The people of the Garden are those who keep coming back without persisting.
try: After your next slip, immediately say astaghfirullah and do one good deed to follow it.

title: Their reward: forgiveness and Gardens. What a reward for workers.
subtitle: Effort that is paid in full
then: This sums up the qualities of the last three verses: giving in all conditions, swallowing anger, pardoning, and returning after sin. Ibn Kathir: {reward}forgiveness and Gardens, forever{/reward}, and {idea}Allah praises this reward{/idea}.
now: Your payslip lists hours worked. This verse calls you a worker too. {idea}Every swallowed word, every pardon, every return after a fall, is logged.{/idea} {reward}And the pay is excellent.{/reward}
old: Only perfect people get Paradise.
new: Paradise is the wage of those who keep working at goodness and keep returning.
try: Pick one of the qualities from verses 134 and 135 and practice it once today.

title: Others before you went through this. Look how it ended.
subtitle: Comfort after the losses at Uhud

row.title: only me
sub: no one ever had it this bad

row.title: a known pattern
sub: others passed through and the end was good

then: After Uhud, where {trap}seventy believers were killed{/trap}, Allah comforts them. Ibn Kathir: earlier nations who followed their prophets also suffered losses, yet {reward}the good end was theirs{/reward}. Travel and see.
now: The diagnosis, the layoff, the miscarriage. You feel like the first person ever to stand in this place. {idea}Others walked here before you, held on to faith, and came through.{/idea}
old: No one has ever gone through something like this.
new: Believers before me faced losses like mine, and the good end was theirs.
try: Read or listen to the story of one person, past or present, who kept faith through a loss like yours.

title: This is a clear statement, guidance, and a lesson.
subtitle: What the Quran does after a loss
then: Right after pointing to history, Allah says the Quran itself is {idea}a clear statement for mankind{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains it shows the true reality of things and gives {reward}guidance for hearts and instruction{/reward} to keep away from what is forbidden.
now: After a hard week you open six tabs looking for an explanation. A podcast, a thread, an article. {idea}The clearest explanation is already on your shelf.{/idea}
old: I need someone to explain why this happened to me.
new: Allah has already given a clear statement that explains, guides, and instructs.
try: When something hard happens this week, read a few verses before reading anything else.

title: Do not weaken, do not grieve. You are higher, if you believe.
subtitle: Standing up again after defeat
then: The believers had just suffered heavy loss. Ibn Kathir: Allah comforts them, {idea}do not become weak because of what you suffered{/idea}, nor grieve, for {reward}the ultimate victory will be yours, O believers{/reward}.
now: You didn't get the promotion. The business failed. Your child is struggling and you feel like you failed them. {idea}Today's score is not your rank.{/idea} {reward}Faith keeps you higher.{/reward}
old: A defeat means I am beneath others now.
new: My rank comes from faith, not from today's result. I don't have to collapse.
try: After your next setback, stand up, make wudu, and pray two rak'ahs before deciding anything.

title: These days We rotate among people.
subtitle: Good days and hard days take turns

row.title: their wound
sub: the other side was hurt too

then: Ibn Kathir explains: if you were wounded, {trap}your enemies were also wounded{/trap}. The days take turns, out of wisdom, so Allah may show who is patient. Hardship {reward}forgives the believers' sins or raises their ranks{/reward}.
now: Last year everything went your way. This year, the car, the job, your health. {idea}Days rotate. That's not abandonment.{/idea} The hard turn is where patience gets seen.
old: When things go badly, it means Allah has turned against me.
new: Days rotate by His wisdom. Hard days reveal patience and are not wasted.
try: Write down one hard thing you are going through and next to it one way it might be refining you.

title: The trial that cleans you is not the one that ends you.
subtitle: Why a believer's loss is not wasted
then: After Uhud the believers had buried seventy of their own. Ibn Kathir explains that the test was {idea}forgiving their sins, or raising their rank by what they lost.{/idea} The other side, when it wins, tends to transgress, and {trap}that conduct leads to its own wearing away.{/trap}
now: The year the business failed. The diagnosis. The exam you studied for and still failed. You sit in the car outside and think it was all wasted. {idea}A loss you carry with faith is still working on you.{/idea}
old: When I lose, I am simply losing.
new: For a believer, even the losing is doing something good inside me.
try: Think of one hard thing from this year. Write one way it made you softer or more honest.

title: Did you think Paradise comes without a test?
subtitle: Effort and patience have to be shown
then: The believers had just come through Uhud. The verse asks them a direct question. Ibn Kathir links it to similar verses: {trap}people who say we believe will be tested.{/trap} {idea}Paradise is reached after Allah makes clear who strives and who stays patient.{/idea}
now: You prayed for a better life and then the hard months came. The night shifts. The relative who will not stop criticizing. You wonder if faith is supposed to feel this heavy. {idea}This might be the road, not a detour from it.{/idea}
old: If I am really on the right path, it should feel easy.
new: The hard part is often proof I am on the path, not off it.
try: Next time something feels hard today, say quietly: this is part of the road.

title: You wished for it. Now it is in front of you.
subtitle: When the thing you asked for arrives
then: Some believers had wished to face the enemy, especially those who missed Badr. At Uhud they saw it with their own eyes. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}do not wish to meet the enemy, ask Allah for well-being, and if you meet them, be patient.{/idea}
now: You said you wanted responsibility. Now you are the manager and the team is falling apart. You said you were ready for marriage, a child, a move abroad. {trap}It looks different up close.{/trap} {idea}Ask for ease, and when it comes anyway, hold steady.{/idea}
old: I am ready for anything, bring it on.
new: I ask Allah for ease, and if hardship comes, I ask Him to keep me steady.
try: Make one short dua today asking for well-being, not for a test.

title: Your faith was never meant to rest on one man.
subtitle: The Messenger ﷺ delivers; Allah remains
then: At Uhud a shout went up that the Prophet ﷺ was killed, and some Muslims lost heart. When he ﷺ did pass away years later, Abu Bakr recited this verse: {idea}whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is alive and will never die.{/idea} 'Umar said his feet could not hold him when he heard it.
now: The teacher who brought you to the deen leaves, or slips. The imam you loved moves cities. Your grandmother, the reason you prayed, dies. {trap}It is tempting to let faith walk out with them.{/trap} {idea}They pointed you to Allah. He is still here.{/idea}
old: If the person who guided me falls away, my faith goes too.
new: People carry the message to me, but my worship is for Allah, who never leaves.
try: Thank one person who taught you about Allah, then thank Allah for sending them.

title: Your last day is written. So what are you working for?
subtitle: The fixed term and the reward you choose

row.title: work for the Hereafter
sub: you get it, plus what is decreed here

then: Ibn Kathir says this verse encourages the fearful: joining the battle or avoiding it neither shortens nor lengthens a life. Then it turns to intention. {idea}Work for the Hereafter brings its reward, along with what is decreed in this life.{/idea} {trap}Work only for this world gets only what Allah decides.{/trap}
now: You keep saying no to the right thing because of what might happen. Speaking up at work. Visiting the sick relative. Starting the charity project. {idea}Your days are already counted.{/idea} The only question left is what they are spent for.
old: If I play it safe, I protect my life.
new: My time is already set, so I can stop bargaining with fear and choose my aim.
try: Pick one task today and quietly make your intention for it the Hereafter.

title: Many before you were hit and did not fold.
subtitle: The steady companions of earlier prophets
then: This came right after the rumor at Uhud made some believers lose heart. Allah points them to the companions of earlier prophets. {idea}They were struck in His way and did not weaken or give in.{/idea} {reward}Allah loves the patient.{/reward}
now: Your community project gets a cruel comment online and half the volunteers vanish. Your family mocks your new habit of praying on time. {idea}You are not the first to be hit.{/idea} Many quiet people kept going long before you.
old: One hard knock and it is fair to give up.
new: I stand in a long line of people who were hit and kept going.
try: Return to one good habit you dropped after a setback. Do it once today.

title: In the hardest moment, they asked forgiveness first.
subtitle: The only words they said

row.title: blame
sub: why is this happening to us

then: This describes the companions of earlier prophets, held up as an example after Uhud. Under attack, {idea}their words were nothing but a prayer{/idea}: forgive our sins and excesses, make our feet firm, help us. {trap}No complaining, no blaming.{/trap}
now: The project collapses and the group chat fills with blame. Whose fault, who dropped the ball. {idea}The prayer here starts with: forgive me, where did I overstep?{/idea} Then: steady me.
old: When things go wrong, I look for who caused it.
new: When things go wrong, I first ask Allah to forgive my part and steady me.
try: Memorize this prayer in your own words and say it once tonight.

title: They asked for steadiness and got both worlds.
subtitle: The answer to that prayer
then: The patient companions of earlier prophets prayed humbly in hardship. {reward}Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter.{/reward} The verse closes: {idea}Allah loves those who do good.{/idea}
now: You kept praying through the hard year without seeing a change. Then one day the job offer, the healing, the peace at home. {idea}Some of it comes here.{/idea} {reward}The better part is kept for later.{/reward}
old: If my reward does not come now, maybe it is not coming.
new: Allah can give some here and keep the best part for the Hereafter.
try: Write down one good thing that came after a hard time you prayed through.

title: Taking advice from those who reject it turns you around.
subtitle: Whose voice you follow after a loss
then: After the defeat at Uhud, the believers were vulnerable. Ibn Kathir says Allah warned them against {trap}obeying the disbelievers and hypocrites, because that obedience leads to ruin{/trap} in this life and the next. {idea}He called them to obey Him and trust Him.{/idea}
now: You are at your lowest and someone says: see, all that praying did nothing, just drop it. A feed full of voices that mock the things you hold. {trap}When you are hurting, it is easy to take directions from the wrong voice.{/trap}
old: When I am down, any advice that sounds confident will do.
new: When I am hurt, I check whose voice is steering me before I follow it.
try: Mute one account or voice that pulls you away from your faith.

title: Not them. Allah is your protector.
subtitle: The best helper, instead of the loudest
then: Right after the warning against obeying the deniers comes the word Nay. {idea}Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers.{/idea} At the end of Uhud, when Abu Sufyan boasted of his idol, the Prophet ﷺ had the companions answer: {reward}Allah is our protector and you have no protector.{/reward}
now: You are scrolling at 2am, looking for anyone who can fix it. A contact, a loan, an influencer's advice. {idea}Before all of them, there is the One who actually protects.{/idea}
old: I need someone powerful on my side to be safe.
new: The most powerful one is already my protector if I turn to Him.
try: Before calling anyone for help today, make a short dua first.

title: Partners with no proof leave hearts full of fear.
subtitle: Why fear entered the other side
then: After Uhud, Allah gave the believers good news. {trap}Fear would be cast into the hearts of their enemies{/trap} because they joined partners with Allah without any authority from Him. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ saying he was {idea}helped by fear placed in his enemies a month's distance away.{/idea}
now: Think of all the things you quietly lean on that have no real power. The lucky ritual, the boss's approval, the bank balance. {trap}The more of them you hold, the more there is to fear losing.{/trap} {idea}One Lord makes a calmer heart.{/idea}
old: The more things I can rely on, the safer I feel.
new: Leaning on things with no real power only multiplies my fear.
try: Notice one worry today and ask: what am I relying on here instead of Allah?

title: Winning, until they ran for the spoils.
subtitle: How Uhud turned, and how Allah forgave
then: The Prophet ﷺ placed archers under 'Abdullah bin Jubayr and told them not to leave their post. When the enemy fled, many shouted {trap}the booty, the booty{/trap} and went down. The cavalry attacked from behind and seventy Muslims were killed. {idea}Yet Allah says He has already forgiven them.{/idea}
now: The team was winning the deal. Then everyone rushed to claim credit and the small checks got skipped. Or the diet was working, until the weekend. {trap}Success is often where you drop your post.{/trap} {idea}And if you did, forgiveness is still open.{/idea}
old: Once I am winning, I can relax the rules.
new: The moment I start winning is the moment to hold my post most carefully.
try: Think of one area where things are going well. Keep the one habit that got you there.

title: Running uphill while he ﷺ called you back.
subtitle: Grief upon grief, so the next grief weighs less
then: When the battle turned, many believers ran up the hillside without looking at anyone, {trap}while the Messenger ﷺ was calling them from behind.{/trap} Allah repaid them with sorrow upon sorrow. The verse gives the reason: {idea}so they would not grieve over what escaped them or what hit them.{/idea}
now: Panic makes you run. You stop answering your mother's calls, stop showing up at the masjid, stop reading. Someone keeps calling you back and you do not turn. {idea}Sometimes the heavier sorrow is what teaches you to stop clutching the smaller one.{/idea}
old: When everything collapses, I just need to get away.
new: In the panic, I listen for the voice calling me back, and I let go of what already passed.
try: Reply to one message you have been avoiding since a hard moment.

title: Some fell asleep in peace; others lay awake doubting Allah.
subtitle: Two groups on the same battlefield

row.title: Abu Talhah
sub: sword kept slipping from his hand

row.title: if only
sub: we would not have died here

then: After the defeat, Allah sent a calm drowsiness on the believers. Abu Talhah said his sword kept falling from his hand. {trap}Another group could not sleep for worry, thinking wrongly of Allah{/trap} and whispering: if we had any say, none of us would be killed here. {idea}The reply: the whole matter belongs to Allah.{/idea}
now: The hospital corridor at 3am. One person in the family sits quietly making dua. Another replays every choice: if we had gone to a different doctor, if we had come earlier. {idea}The decree was Allah's. The test is what it shows in your heart.{/idea}
old: If I had controlled every detail, this would not have happened.
new: I do my part, then rest the outcome with Allah, who owns the whole matter.
try: Catch one if-only thought today and replace it with: the matter is Allah's.

title: One slip led to another, and Allah still forgave.
subtitle: How a fall is set up earlier
then: Some believers turned back at Uhud. The verse says Shaytan made them slip {trap}because of some of what they had earned before.{/trap} A saying of the early Muslims: one reward of a good deed is another good deed after it. {reward}Yet Allah had already forgiven them,{/reward} and 'Uthman later refused to be blamed for what Allah forgave.
now: The big failure rarely comes from nowhere. It is the skipped prayers, the small lies, the late nights scrolling. Then one day you fold under pressure. {idea}Small choices set up big moments.{/idea} {reward}And forgiveness is still there after.{/reward}
old: My big failures come out of nowhere.
new: My big moments are shaped by small earlier choices, and Allah forgives the one who turns back.
try: Pick one small good deed and do it today, to make the next one easier.

title: If they had stayed home, they would still be alive?
subtitle: The thought that only grows the grief
then: Some said about those who died travelling for trade or in battle: {trap}had they stayed with us, they would not have died.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says Allah lets that thought sit in their hearts so their grief grows. {idea}It is Allah who gives life and causes death.{/idea}
now: A friend dies in a car crash on a trip. At the funeral someone says: why did he go, he should have stayed. The family hears it for years. {trap}That sentence only adds pain.{/trap} {idea}His term was written, wherever he was.{/idea}
old: If they had made a different choice, they would still be here.
new: Their time was set by Allah; blaming the trip only deepens the wound.
try: If you comfort someone grieving this week, avoid if-only words. Say a dua for the one who died.

title: Mercy is worth more than everything they pile up.
subtitle: Dying on the right path is not a loss
then: The believers were hearing the hypocrites mourn their dead as people who lost out. {idea}Death or martyrdom in Allah's way brings His forgiveness and mercy.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says this is {reward}better than staying in this life with its short delights.{/reward}
now: You see people your age with the house, the car, the trips abroad. You wonder if your quieter, careful life is losing the race. {reward}Forgiveness and mercy from Allah outweigh every pile.{/reward}
old: The one who collects the most has won.
new: The one who leaves forgiven has won more than any collector.
try: Ask Allah for forgiveness and mercy once today, by name, as the thing you want most.

title: However you go, you go to Him.
subtitle: Every death ends at the same gathering
then: This closes the reply to those who said staying home would have saved their brothers. {idea}Whether you die or are killed, you will be gathered to Allah.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds that He will reward good deeds and hold people to account for evil ones.
now: You worry about how it will happen. The flight, the illness, the night drive home. {idea}The way out matters less than where every way leads.{/idea} What you bring with you is the part you can work on today.
old: I mostly worry about how and when I will die.
new: I care more about what I bring when I am gathered to Allah.
try: Do one deed today you would be glad to arrive with.

title: Gentleness is why they stayed around him ﷺ.
subtitle: Pardon, consult, decide, then trust
then: This came after Uhud, where some had disobeyed and fled. Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that {idea}by His mercy he was gentle with them{/idea}, and {trap}had he been harsh, they would have scattered.{/trap} He ﷺ often consulted his Companions, as he did before Badr and Uhud.
now: Your teenager crashed the car. Your colleague missed the deadline that cost the team. You want to shout and shut them out. {idea}Pardon, ask Allah to forgive them, and still ask for their opinion next time.{/idea} Then make the call and trust Allah.
old: When people let me down, being harsh keeps them in line.
new: Mercy keeps people close; I pardon, still involve them, decide, and trust Allah.
try: Ask the opinion of someone who recently let you down, on one small decision.

title: If Allah helps you, no one can beat you.
subtitle: And if He does not, who else could
then: Right after telling the Prophet ﷺ to trust Allah once he decides, the verse widens it to all believers. Ibn Kathir links it to an earlier line: {idea}there is no victory except from Allah.{/idea} {trap}If He leaves you, no one after Him can help.{/trap}
now: You have the right degree, the right referral, the right savings. You still feel fragile. Or you have none of it and feel hopeless. {idea}Neither list decides the outcome.{/idea} Do your part and lean on the One who does.
old: My success depends on having enough resources and contacts.
new: Resources are tools; the help itself comes from Allah.
try: Before your next important task, say: I rely on Allah. Then begin.

title: Whatever you secretly take, you carry on that Day.
subtitle: A prophet does not betray a trust

row.title: a rumor
sub: maybe the Prophet ﷺ took it

row.title: no prophet betrays
sub: the one who does carries it

then: Ibn 'Abbas said this was revealed about a red robe missing from the spoils of Badr, when {trap}some said the Prophet ﷺ might have taken it.{/trap} The verse clears him: {idea}it is not for a prophet to betray a trust.{/idea} Whoever does will bring what he took on the Day.
now: The office supplies that go home. The extra hours on the timesheet. The shared family money no one is tracking. {trap}It feels too small to count.{/trap} {idea}Every hidden taking is something you will carry.{/idea}
old: Small things no one notices do not really count.
new: What I take in secret I will carry in the open.
try: Return or pay back one small thing that is not fully yours.

title: Chasing His pleasure is not the same as earning His anger.
subtitle: Two directions that never meet
then: This follows the verse about betraying a trust. {idea}Is the one who follows Allah's pleasure like the one who brings His anger on himself?{/idea} The question answers itself. {trap}One path ends in a wretched place.{/trap}
now: You watch someone cut corners and still get the promotion. You start to wonder if honesty is just slower. {idea}The verse says the two are not the same, even if today's scoreboard looks equal.{/idea}
old: If cheaters get ahead too, being honest makes no difference.
new: The one seeking Allah's pleasure and the one earning His anger are never equal.
try: Choose the honest option in one small choice today, even if it costs a little.

title: People stand at different levels with Allah.
subtitle: He sees exactly what each one does
then: After contrasting those who seek Allah's pleasure with those who earn His anger, the verse adds: {idea}they are in degrees with Allah{/idea}, and He sees what they do. {reward}No effort is missed.{/reward}
now: Nobody saw you stay late to help the new hire, or sit with your father at the clinic all morning. Your post got no likes. {idea}Allah saw it, and He ranks by what He sees.{/idea}
old: If no one notices my effort, it does not count.
new: Allah sees every effort and places each person where they truly stand.
try: Do one good thing today that no one will see.

title: A Messenger from among them was the great gift.
subtitle: Four things he ﷺ brought
then: Even after the pain of Uhud, Allah reminds the believers of {reward}the great favor He gave them{/reward}: a Messenger ﷺ from their own people. He recited the verses, purified them, and taught the Book and wisdom, {trap}though before that they were in clear error.{/trap}
now: After a hard week you list everything that went wrong. The bills, the argument, the bad news. {reward}The list rarely includes that you have the Quran in your pocket and a Prophet's ﷺ example to follow.{/reward}
old: When life is hard, I mostly count what is missing.
new: Even on hard days, guidance itself is the biggest gift I hold.
try: Read one hadith or one verse today and thank Allah for it by name.

title: Where did this come from? Look at yourselves.
subtitle: The honest answer to why it went wrong
then: At Badr the Muslims had killed seventy and captured seventy. At Uhud, a year later, they lost seventy. They asked: {trap}how did this happen to us?{/trap} The answer: {idea}it is from yourselves.{/idea} Scholars Ibn Kathir cites point to the archers disobeying the order to stay at their post.
now: The relationship ends, the savings are gone, the grade is low, and your first question is whose fault it is. {idea}The braver question is: what did I do here?{/idea} It is not to crush yourself. It is the only part you can fix.
old: When things go wrong, something outside me caused it.
new: I first ask what part came from my own choices, because that part I can change.
try: Think of one recent setback. Write one thing you did that contributed to it.

title: What hit you that day still came by His permission.
subtitle: Your fault, and still within His plan
then: The verse before said the loss came from their own mistake. This one adds: {idea}it happened by Allah's leave, out of His wisdom{/idea}, to bring out the believers who were patient and not shaken. {trap}Their error was real.{/trap} So was His purpose.
now: You made a bad call at work and it cost you. It was your mistake. {idea}And Allah still allowed it, and there is something in it for you.{/idea} How you carry the fallout shows who you are.
old: If it was my fault, Allah has nothing to do with it.
new: My mistake is mine, and Allah still placed a test and a purpose in it.
try: Ask Allah in one line to make your latest mistake a lesson, not a wound.

title: If we knew there would be a fight, we would come.
subtitle: Excuses that the mouth says and the heart does not
then: Before Uhud, a group turned back to Madinah with 'Abdullah bin Ubayy. Some believers urged them to come back and at least defend. They said: {trap}if we knew there would be fighting, we would follow you{/trap}, though an army was clearly marching. Ibn Kathir notes {idea}a person can be closer to disbelief one day and to faith another.{/idea}
now: The friend who says: if I knew it was serious, I would have come to the hospital. Your own: I would help, I just did not know it was this week. {trap}Sometimes we knew.{/trap} {idea}Each day you are moving one way or the other.{/idea}
old: My excuse is believable, so it is fine.
new: Allah knows what is behind my excuse, and each choice moves me toward or away from faith.
try: Notice one excuse you give today. Ask if it is the real reason.

title: Then keep death away from yourselves, if you can.
subtitle: The challenge to those who stayed home
then: Those who stayed back said about the martyrs: {trap}if they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed.{/trap} Jabir said this was revealed about 'Abdullah bin Ubayy. The reply: {idea}then push death away from yourselves, if you are truthful.{/idea}
now: Someone took a risk for something good and it went badly. You are on the sofa saying: I told them not to. {trap}It feels wise to say from a safe seat.{/trap} {idea}Your own seat is not as safe as it feels.{/idea}
old: I was smart to stay out of it.
new: Staying back does not buy me more life, so I should not judge those who stepped forward.
try: Say one kind word today about someone who tried something good and failed.

title: Do not think of them as dead.
subtitle: The martyrs are alive with their Lord

picture.label: What the eyes see vs. the truth

row.title: Allah spoke to him
sub: he asked to tell those behind

then: These verses were revealed about the martyrs of Uhud. The Prophet ﷺ saw Jabir sad because his father was killed and left debts and children. {idea}He ﷺ told him Allah had spoken to his father directly{/idea}, and his father asked that those left behind be told. {reward}They are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.{/reward}
now: You stand by a grave and it feels like the end of the story. The empty chair at Eid, the number you cannot delete. {idea}For those who die in Allah's way, the story did not end at the grave.{/idea}
old: When someone dies, they are simply gone.
new: For those who give their lives for Allah, death opens into life with Him.
try: Make dua today for someone you have lost, using their name.

title: They are happy, and they are thinking of you.
subtitle: Good news sent back for those still here

row.title: if only they knew
sub: so they do not hold back

then: The martyrs of Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ said, wished their brothers knew what Allah had given them, {idea}so they would not hold back from striving.{/idea} Allah said He would convey it for them. {reward}They rejoice that those who follow will have no fear and no grief.{/reward}
now: You feel guilty laughing again after the funeral. Or you feel far from the person you lost. {idea}The ones who left on the right path are not jealous of your life. They want you to reach where they are.{/idea}
old: Those who passed are gone and cut off from us.
new: Those who passed in Allah's way are rejoicing and hoping the same for us.
try: Do one good deed today with the intention of reaching the people you lost.

title: Not one believer's reward is wasted.
subtitle: The good news they rejoice over
then: The martyrs' joy continues here. {reward}They rejoice in favor and bounty from Allah{/reward}, and {idea}that Allah does not let the reward of the believers be lost.{/idea}
now: Years of caring for a sick parent. The night prayers no one knew about. The patience with a difficult child. You wonder if any of it was counted. {idea}It was. Not one bit lost.{/idea}
old: So much of what I do disappears without a trace.
new: Allah keeps every believer's reward; none of it is lost.
try: Remind yourself of one quiet sacrifice and tell Allah: I did it for You.

title: Still wounded, they answered the call again.
subtitle: Responding after you have been hurt

row.title: the call
sub: of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ

then: This describes believers who {idea}responded to Allah and the Messenger ﷺ after injury had struck them.{/idea} Their wounds from Uhud were still fresh. {reward}For those of them who did good and feared Allah, there is a great reward.{/reward}
now: You are still hurt from the last time you helped. The volunteering that burned you out. The family member who did not say thank you. A new call comes. {idea}You do not need to be fully healed to answer it.{/idea}
old: I will do good again once I have fully recovered.
new: Answering the call while still hurt is part of what makes it great.
try: Say yes to one small good request today, even though you feel tired.

title: They warned, be afraid. It only grew their faith.
subtitle: Allah is enough for us
then: The same wounded believers were told: {trap}people have gathered against you, so fear them.{/trap} Instead of breaking, {idea}their faith increased{/idea}, and they said: {reward}Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.{/reward}
now: The news says layoffs are coming. The doctor says the results look worrying. The group chat is full of panic. {idea}Say it slowly: Hasbuna Allahu wa ni'mal wakeel.{/idea} Then take the next sensible step.
old: When the threat is big, my fear should be big.
new: When the threat is big, I remember Allah is enough, and my faith grows.
try: Say Hasbuna Allahu wa ni'mal wakeel the next time worrying news reaches you.

title: They went out afraid of nothing and came back blessed.
subtitle: No harm touched them
then: After saying Allah is enough for us, {reward}they returned with favor and bounty from Allah, and no harm touched them.{/reward} {idea}They had followed what pleases Allah{/idea}, and He is the Owner of great bounty.
now: You went to the hard meeting, made the honest call, visited the relative everyone warned you about. The disaster you dreaded did not come. {reward}You came home lighter.{/reward}
old: Doing the right thing under pressure will cost me.
new: When I follow Allah's pleasure, I often return with more than I risked.
try: Do the one task you have been avoiding out of fear, and leave the result with Allah.

title: That fear in your chest is Shaytan's work.
subtitle: Fear Allah, not his allies
then: This explains the scare the believers had just been given. {trap}It is only Shaytan who frightens you with his allies.{/trap} {idea}So do not fear them. Fear Me, if you are believers.{/idea}
now: You are afraid to pray at work, afraid to say no to the haram deal, afraid of being laughed at. {trap}That fear is whispered.{/trap} {idea}Fearing Allah first makes the other fears shrink.{/idea}
old: Being scared of people who could hurt me is just realism.
new: Much of that fear is whispered to stop me; fearing Allah first sets me free.
try: Name one fear of people that is stopping a good deed, then do the deed anyway.

title: Do not let their rush away from faith break you.
subtitle: They cannot harm Allah at all
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was so eager for people's good that {trap}he became sad when they defied and rejected.{/trap} Allah comforts him: {idea}do not let them grieve you, they will never harm Allah at all.{/idea}
now: Your brother stops praying. A friend you brought to the masjid walks away and mocks it. You feel it as your failure. {idea}Care, pray for them, keep the door open.{/idea} But their choice does not harm Allah, and it does not have to crush you.
old: If someone I love leaves the faith, it is on me.
new: I keep caring and praying, but their choice cannot harm Allah and does not have to break me.
try: Make a short dua for one person who has drifted, then let the worry rest.

title: Trading faith away harms only the trader.
subtitle: A bad bargain that Allah does not feel
then: Right after comforting the Prophet ﷺ about those rushing into disbelief, Allah describes people who {trap}bought disbelief at the price of faith.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says {idea}they will not harm Allah at all; they only harm themselves.{/idea}
now: You quietly trade your prayer time for overtime, your honesty for a better deal, your values to fit in with a new crowd. It feels like a small swap. {idea}Allah does not lose from it. You do.{/idea}
old: Giving up a bit of my faith is my business and costs no one.
new: When I trade faith away, I am the only one who pays.
try: Name one thing you have been trading your faith for. Take one step back from it today.

title: Getting away with it is not the same as being okay.
subtitle: When delay is not a sign of approval
then: Allah warns those who reject Him: {trap}do not think the delay in your punishment is good for you.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to verses about people given wealth and children who think it means Allah is pleased. {idea}The delay only lets the sin grow, unless they turn back.{/idea}
now: You cheated on the test and passed. You lied to your boss and nothing happened. Months go by and you start to think it was fine. {idea}The quiet is not a verdict. It is time given to repent.{/idea}
old: If nothing bad happened, it must not have been so bad.
new: Time without consequences is a chance to turn back, not proof I was right.
try: Think of one wrong you got away with. Ask Allah's forgiveness for it tonight.

title: Hard days sort the true from the pretending.
subtitle: Allah will not leave things mixed forever
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to Uhud. {idea}Allah lets a calamity come so that His friend becomes known and His enemy exposed.{/idea} Believers showed patience and firmness; {trap}hypocrites showed their retreat.{/trap} People cannot see the unseen; Allah reveals it to whom He chooses of His messengers.
now: A crisis hits the family business, and you find out who stays to help and who disappears. It also shows you yourself. {idea}Hard days are a mirror.{/idea} The aim is not to judge others, but to see where you stand.
old: I already know who is real and who is not.
new: Trials reveal hearts, starting with mine, and the unseen belongs to Allah.
try: Ask yourself: in the last hard moment, how did I act? Write one honest line.

title: What you hold back will hang around your neck.
subtitle: Stinginess looks like gain, but it is loss
then: Ibn Kathir says the miser should not think piling up wealth helps him; {trap}it harms his religion and his worldly life.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ recited this verse about wealth whose zakah is not paid. {idea}And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth.{/idea}
now: Payday comes. You see the fundraiser link in the family chat and scroll past. You tell yourself you need a cushion. {trap}What you grip will not stay with you.{/trap} {idea}It all goes back to its Owner anyway.{/idea}
old: Keeping my money is what keeps me secure.
new: Everything returns to Allah; only what I give goes ahead of me.
try: Give a small amount today to someone in need, even if it feels inconvenient.

title: Allah heard them mock Him as poor.
subtitle: Every word is recorded
then: Ibn 'Abbas said when the verse about lending Allah a goodly loan came down, {trap}some in Madinah mocked: has your Lord become poor?{/trap} Allah replied that He heard them. {idea}He would record what they said{/idea}, along with the killing of prophets by their forebears.
now: A joke at the dinner table: why does God need my charity? Or a sarcastic comment under a fundraising post. {idea}Words about Allah are not small talk. They are written down.{/idea} The giving is for you, not for Him.
old: A sarcastic line about religion is just a joke.
new: Every word I say about Allah is heard and recorded, so I speak with care.
try: Next time religion comes up in a joke, stay quiet or change the subject kindly.

title: What your hands sent ahead is what you meet.
subtitle: Allah is never unjust to anyone
then: This closes the warning to those who mocked Allah and killed prophets. Ibn Kathir says it is said to them in rebuke: {trap}this is because of what your hands sent before you.{/trap} {idea}Allah is never unjust to His servants.{/idea}
now: Every message you send, every hour you spend, every coin you give or keep is going on ahead of you. {idea}You will meet it again.{/idea} The good news: you can send good ahead starting today.
old: What happens to me in the end is out of my hands.
new: My hands are sending things ahead each day, and Allah will treat me with perfect justice.
try: Send one good thing ahead today on purpose: a kind word, a gift, a prayer.

title: Proof was never really the problem.
subtitle: Demanding a sign you would ignore anyway
then: Some claimed Allah told them to believe no messenger until he brought an offering consumed by fire from the sky. {idea}Allah replied: messengers came before me with clear proofs, and with what you ask for.{/idea} {trap}So why did you kill them, if you are truthful?{/trap}
now: You say you will start praying once you feel it. Once you get a sign. Once your questions are all answered. {trap}Sometimes the demand for proof is a way to delay.{/trap} {idea}Ask yourself what would really change.{/idea}
old: I will commit once I get the right sign.
new: Often I already have enough; what I lack is the will to act.
try: Do one act of worship today you have been putting off until you feel ready.

title: If they deny you, they denied the best before you.
subtitle: Comfort for the rejected messenger ﷺ
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah comforts the Prophet ﷺ here: {idea}do not be sad that they deny you{/idea}, for messengers before you were denied too. {trap}They came with clear proofs, scriptures and an enlightening Book, and were still rejected.{/trap}
now: You shared something true and good, and people laughed, or unfollowed, or argued. You start to doubt yourself. {idea}Being rejected is not proof you were wrong.{/idea} The best people in history were rejected too.
old: If people reject what I say, I must be wrong.
new: Rejection happened to the messengers; it does not decide what is true.
try: Keep doing one good thing you do quietly, even though someone mocked it.

title: Every soul will taste death. Then the real pay.
subtitle: Who actually wins
then: Ibn Kathir says this verse comforts all creation: everyone dies, and only Allah remains. {idea}Full payment comes on the Day of Resurrection.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}a whip's length of space in Paradise is better than the world and all it holds.{/reward}
now: The promotion, the wedding photos, the new car, the number of followers. All of it feels like the scoreboard. {idea}The real scoreboard opens after the last breath.{/idea} Qatadah said: take obedience to Allah from this delight while you can.
old: Success means winning in this life.
new: Success is being kept from the Fire and let into Paradise; the rest passes.
try: Look at your plans for this week and add one thing that counts for the Hereafter.

title: You will be tested and you will hear hurtful words.
subtitle: Patience and taqwa are the strong choice
then: Early in Madinah, 'Abdullah bin Ubayy insulted the Prophet ﷺ when he came to a gathering and recited Quran. Sa'd bin 'Ubadah asked him ﷺ to pardon him, and {idea}he ﷺ forgave him.{/idea} The Companions used to {reward}bear the harm and forgive{/reward}, as this verse commanded.
now: The comment under your post. The relative who mocks your hijab or beard. The coworker's joke about your fasting. {trap}You will hear it.{/trap} {idea}Patience and mindfulness of Allah are not weakness. The verse calls them resolve.{/idea}
old: If I do not hit back, I look weak.
new: Patience with Allah in mind is the strongest response I have.
try: Next time someone says something hurtful, pause and say nothing for ten seconds.

title: They were trusted to share the truth and sold it cheap.
subtitle: Knowledge is meant to be made clear

row.title: share what helps
sub: it was given as a trust

then: Allah took a covenant from those given scripture to make it clear and not hide it. {trap}They threw it behind their backs for a small gain.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}a warning for every scholar not to do the same{/idea}, and to spread beneficial knowledge.
now: You know the truth in a family dispute but stay quiet because it is awkward. A friend asks you a question about the deen and you brush it off. {trap}Silence can be a small price too.{/trap} {idea}Share what you know, gently.{/idea}
old: What I know is mine to share or keep as I like.
new: Useful truth I know is a trust; I should make it clear, not sell it for comfort.
try: Share one beneficial thing you learned this week with someone who would benefit.

title: Loving praise for what you never did.
subtitle: A false image is no shelter

row.title: want praise
sub: for what they did not do

then: Ibn Kathir says this is about those who show off and claim deeds they did not do. Abu Sa'id said some hypocrites stayed back from battle, then {trap}swore excuses and wanted praise for what they did not do.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}one who claims what he was not given is like one wearing two robes of falsehood.{/idea}
now: The group project where you let people think the idea was yours. The photo that makes your charity look bigger than it was. The CV line stretched a little. {trap}The praise feels good.{/trap} {idea}It is a robe made of nothing.{/idea}
old: A little exaggeration about myself harms no one.
new: Praise for what I did not do is a costume that will not protect me.
try: Correct one place where people credit you for something you did not fully do.

title: Everything belongs to Him, and He can do anything.
subtitle: The reason no show-off escapes
then: This comes right after the warning to those who love praise for what they did not do. Ibn Kathir says: {idea}He is the Owner of everything, able to do all things, and nothing escapes His might.{/idea} {trap}So fear Him and do not defy Him.{/trap}
now: You polish your reputation online, at work, in the family. It feels like protection. {idea}The One who owns the heavens and the earth sees past every image.{/idea} That is humbling, and also freeing.
old: If people think well of me, I am safe.
new: Only the Owner of everything decides what happens to me, so I stop performing for others.
try: Do one good deed today and tell no one about it.

title: Look up. The sky and the night are signs.
subtitle: The verse the Prophet ﷺ recited looking at the sky
then: Ibn 'Abbas stayed one night at his aunt Maymunah's home. In the last third of the night, {idea}the Prophet ﷺ stood up, looked at the sky and recited this verse{/idea}, then made wudu and prayed. Ibn Kathir says he ﷺ used to recite these closing ten verses when he rose to pray at night.
now: You walk to the bus with your head in your phone. The sunrise happens anyway. The days get shorter in winter and you only notice the heating bill. {idea}Every change of light is a sign, waiting for someone to look.{/idea}
old: The sky and the seasons are just background.
new: The sky, the earth, and the turning of night and day are signs pointing me to Allah.
try: Tonight, step outside or to a window, look at the sky for one minute, and recite this verse.

title: Standing, sitting, lying down, they remember Him.
subtitle: Reflection that ends in a prayer
then: Ibn Kathir says these people {idea}remember Allah in every state, in heart and speech{/idea}, and reflect on creation. Their conclusion becomes a prayer: {reward}You did not make this without purpose, glory to You, so save us from the Fire.{/reward} Creation in truth means deeds will be repaid.
now: Lying in bed, unable to sleep. Sitting in traffic. Standing in the queue at the pharmacy. {idea}Each one can be a moment of remembering.{/idea} You do not need a prayer mat to think about the One who made it all.
old: Remembering Allah is for when I am praying.
new: I can remember Allah in every position and moment, and let my thinking turn into prayer.
try: Say Subhanak, Rabbana once each while standing, sitting and lying down today.

title: The real disgrace is the one in front of everyone.
subtitle: Their prayer to be saved from it
then: The people of understanding continue their prayer. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}whoever enters the Fire is disgraced before all people on the Day of Gathering{/trap}, and no one can save the wrongdoers from Allah. {idea}So they ask to be kept from it.{/idea}
now: You dread being embarrassed: a mistake in the meeting, a bad photo, a rumor at school. {idea}This prayer shifts the fear to the shame that actually lasts{/idea}, and turns that fear into asking for help.
old: The worst thing is being embarrassed in front of people.
new: The shame I should really fear is on that Day, and I can ask Allah to protect me from it now.
try: Add to your next prayer: Our Lord, do not disgrace me on the Day.

title: We heard the call to faith, and we answered.
subtitle: Then forgive us, and let us die with the good
then: Ibn Kathir says the caller to faith is the Messenger ﷺ. {idea}They accepted his call and followed him.{/idea} On account of that faith, they ask Allah to forgive their sins, cover their misdeeds in private, and {reward}join them with the righteous at death.{/reward}
now: You heard the call too. Maybe from a parent, a friend, a video at 2am. You answered, imperfectly. {idea}This prayer lets you stand on that answer and ask for the rest.{/idea}
old: I am not good enough to ask Allah for much.
new: I answered the call to faith, so I can ask Allah to forgive me and let me die among the good.
try: Make this dua once today: forgive us, cover our faults, and let us die with the righteous.

title: You never break a promise, so give us what You promised.
subtitle: Asking with confidence
then: The prayer ends here. Ibn Kathir prefers the meaning: {idea}grant us what You promised by the words of Your messengers.{/idea} They ask not to be disgraced before all creation, {reward}for the promise of Allah will certainly come to pass.{/reward}
now: People break promises to you. The landlord, the friend who said they would come, the company that promised a raise. {idea}Allah never does.{/idea} So you can ask Him as someone holding a promise.
old: I hope Allah might reward me, but I am not sure I can ask.
new: Allah never breaks His promise, so I ask for it with trust.
try: When you make dua today, add: You never break Your promise.

title: Their Lord answered: no one's work is lost, man or woman.
subtitle: Revealed after Umm Salamah asked a question

row.title: gardens
sub: for those harmed in My way

then: Umm Salamah said: {trap}O Messenger of Allah, Allah does not mention women in connection with the Hijrah.{/trap} Allah sent this down. {idea}I will not let the work of any of you be lost, male or female; you are of one another.{/idea} The Ansar said she was the first woman to migrate to them.
now: The mother up at night with the baby. The daughter who left her city to care for her father. The woman whose sacrifice never gets a speech at the wedding. {idea}Allah named it in His Book: not one deed lost.{/idea}
old: My quiet efforts at home do not count like other people's.
new: Allah does not lose the work of any worker, man or woman.
try: Thank one woman in your life today for a sacrifice she has made.

title: Do not be fooled by how freely they move.
subtitle: Wealth and ease in the land
then: After the believers' long prayer, Allah tells them: {trap}do not be deceived by the free movement of those who disbelieve.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they are enjoying delights now, but {idea}they are only being given time.{/idea}
now: You scroll past someone living the dream: travel, money, no rules, no prayer. A thought creeps in that maybe they figured it out. {idea}Ease on the surface is not a verdict.{/idea} Watch your own heart instead of their feed.
old: People with easy, free lives must be doing something right.
new: Freedom and comfort here are not proof of anything; the end is what counts.
try: Unfollow or mute one account that makes you envy a life without faith.

title: A little enjoyment, and then a bad place to rest.
subtitle: How short the good time is
then: This finishes the thought of the verse before. Their ease is {trap}a brief enjoyment, then their final home is Hell, a wretched resting place.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to other verses: {idea}We let them enjoy a little while.{/idea}
now: The weekend that turns into regret. The money spent fast that leaves nothing. {idea}Most of what dazzles is short.{/idea} The question is where you rest at the end.
old: If I enjoy myself now, I can worry about the end later.
new: Short enjoyment is not worth a bad ending; I want to rest well at the end.
try: Before one indulgence today, ask: will this help or hurt where I end up?

title: What is with Allah is better for the righteous.
subtitle: A welcome prepared by Him
then: After describing the short enjoyment of the deniers, Allah turns to those with taqwa: {reward}gardens with rivers, to dwell in forever, a hosting from Allah.{/reward} Abu Ad-Darda' used to say {idea}death is better for every believer{/idea}, citing that what is with Allah is best for the righteous.
now: You turned down the deal. You kept your hijab at the interview. You left the party early to pray. It cost you something. {reward}A welcome is being prepared by Allah for exactly that.{/reward}
old: Holding back for Allah's sake means I miss out.
new: What I hold back for Allah is replaced by something far better with Him.
try: Think of one thing you gave up for Allah and say: what is with Allah is better.

title: Some of the People of the Book believed, humbly.
subtitle: They did not sell Allah's verses cheap

row.title: a brother of yours
sub: the Prophet ﷺ prayed for him

then: After many verses about those who hid the truth, Allah says {idea}some of the People of the Book believe, humbly, and do not sell His verses for a small price.{/idea} When Ja'far recited Surah Maryam to An-Najashi, he wept. When he died, {reward}the Prophet ﷺ said a brother of yours in Ethiopia has died, and led the funeral prayer.{/reward}
now: It is easy to lump people together and write them off. The verse refuses to. {idea}It names the humble ones and honors them.{/idea} Ask yourself whether you hold the truth with the same humility.
old: Those groups are all the same.
new: Allah sees and honors each humble, sincere person, wherever they started.
try: Catch yourself if you generalize about any group today, and replace it with a fair word.

title: Be patient, outlast, stay at your post, and fear Allah.
subtitle: The last verse of Ali 'Imran
then: The surah that began after Uhud closes here. Al-Hasan said believers are told to {idea}hold to their religion in comfort and hardship until they die as Muslims.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ described perfect wudu when it is hard, many steps to the masjid, and {reward}waiting for prayer after prayer: this is the ribat.{/reward}
now: The cold-water wudu on a winter morning. The walk to the masjid when the car is in the shop. Sitting a few minutes after Maghrib, already waiting for Isha. {idea}That is staying at your post.{/idea}
old: Holding firm is something heroes do in big moments.
new: Holding firm is daily: patience, staying power, and keeping my post at each prayer.
try: After your next prayer, sit for two quiet minutes before getting up.
